News.title: Tories will cut student loans to foreign students saving British taxpayers £1 billion
News.content:
Plan to slash cash to foreign students will free up cash for tax cuts







Next

THE TORIES will cut student loans to foreign students – saving British taxpayers nearly £1 billion a year.

Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith will announce the plan at Tory Party conference in Birmingham tomorrow [MON] – alongside measures to cut Britain’s bloated benefits bill.

Currently, around 20 per cent of UK student loans go to foreign students – up from 10 per cent a decade ago. This amounts to about £4 billion a year.



But foreign students are less likely than British students to pay their loan back.



Only half (51 per cent) of foreign students pay the cash back, compared to 68 per cent of Brits.

Mr Griffith told The Sun on Sunday: “Labour is handing out £4 billion a year in student loans to foreign nationals, and barely half of it is ever paid back.

“A Conservative government will turn off the tap and save £900 million a year.”

The Tories will end access to UK student loans for foreign nations from non EU countries.

Under the terms of the Brexit deal, EU citizens with settled status would still be allowed to get the loans.

Tory shadow education secretary Laura Trott said too many foreign students are abusing Britain’s generous student loans system.



She said: “We want to welcome international students to our universities, but not at the expense of British students and taxpayers.

“Repayment rates are lower among overseas borrowers, leaving British taxpayers to pick up the bill. This is not fair.”

The Tories say they will save an estimated £900 million a year with the policy.

Kemi Badenoch is expected to use the flagship speech to announce the abolition of inheritance tax, as The Sun on Sunday exclusively revealed last month.

News.title: Flames tear through garage and destroy family home after car that failed MOT catches fire
News.content:
'SOUL-DESTROYING' Flames tear through garage and destroy family home after car that failed MOT catches fire







Next

A HUGE blaze has torn through a family’s home after a car that failed its MOT caught alight.

Fire crews, including 10 fire engines, descended on a car workshop in Little Walden, Essex shortly after midday on Friday.



In dramatic images, firefighters can be seen battling the flames as huge plumes of black smoke billowed into the air.

The fire service urged local residents to keep their windows and doors shut as they worked to bring the fire under control.



The blaze completely destroyed the workshop, two cars and an adjoining home which were reduced to burnt-out shells.

Essex County Fire and Rescue said the fire was accidental after a motor caught alight on an MOT ramp at D&K Vehicle Services.

Callum Ogborn, a mechanic one of the firm’s four directors, told the BBC the fire had spread from a 1990s petrol vehicle imported from Japan.

It had failed its MOT test just four days earlier.



“I did try to extinguish the flames but unfortunately it didn’t do much in the way of putting the fire out and it just went up so quickly, once it had started there was just no stopping it,” he told the broadcaster.

“Two vehicles are a complete loss and there are five or six in the car park that have suffered damage due to the extreme heat.”

He added that his father had converted the barn into his home and family business after taking on the company “from the day he left high school”.

The family had “more or less been building from the ground up for the last 10 years”.

“My dad and stepmum have painstakingly renovated the adjoining barn over the same time period at weekends and evenings, so it was absolutely soul-destroying,” he said.



In a statement on Facebook, the workshop said the fire “spread far too quickly for us to manage”, calling it “absolutely devastating” to watch.

They added they had “lost the entire workshop and all the equipment”.

The firm said they “aren’t sure what the next steps are going to be” and urged those with a vehicle at the site to get in touch.

Andy Message, Group Manager for Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said: “Firefighters have worked extremely hard with the support of crews from neighbouring counties in Suffolk and Cambridgeshire to extinguish the fire.

“We are now in a position to scale the incident down and have crews remaining to monitor and cool hotspots.”



The fire service said on Friday: “Firefighters are currently tackling a fire on Little Walden Road in Little Walden.

“There is a lot of smoke coming from the incident, please keep all your windows and doors shut.

“It is a fire which is affecting a workshop and a nearby property.

“Due to poor water supply, six fire engines and a water bowser have been called to help tackle the fire.”

News.title: Red ‘danger to life’ alert issued as Spain holiday hotspot braces for ‘mini-hurricane’ with horror floods & 70mph winds
News.content:
RAGING TEMPEST Red ‘danger to life’ alert issued as Spain holiday hotspot braces for ‘mini-hurricane’ with horror floods & 70mph winds







Next

A RED “danger to life” warning has hit a Spanish holiday hotspot as a “mini-hurricane” threatens the region with torrential downpours and gale force winds.

Catalonia‘s president warned – “this is not a joke” – as the dire alert was issued for Barcelona and Girona, pleading with residents to respect the strict restrictions.



The state meteorological agency Aemet have issued a rare red weather which will strictly be in place from 9pm on Saturday evening until midday on Sunday.

Forecasters are expecting up to 90mm of rain to fall in just an hour, with total rainfall potentially exceeding 200mm in just six hours.





Officials say there is a real risk of flash flooding as the already saturated rivers may not be able to handle the impending barrage.

Severe overnight storms could bring intense lightning, tornadoes, waterspouts, and gale-force winds exceeding 120 km/h, with conditions expected to peak around midnight.

After midnight, the red alert will extend to cover large parts of northern Catalunya, including Girona, Mataro, Figueres and the Costa Brava towards the French border.

Movement across 20 regions covering coastal and hinterland areas of Tarragona, Barcelona and Girona will be restricted as long as the warning is in place.



President Salvador Illa said the situation is “very complex”.

Local authorities are preparing to send an emergency alert message directly to mobile phones in the highest-risk areas this afternoon.

Heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected across the Balearics overnight with an orange weather warning put in place.



Today’s warning comes just days after torrential rains and flash floods battered Barcelona, sparking flight chaos and leaving holidaymakers stranded.

The thunderstorms raged mostly in the northeast and northwest.

Overnight, surprise flash flooding in Madrigueras left one elderly woman dead and forced the rescue of 90 people – many of who were trapped in their homes.



Severe thunderstorms and torrential rains lashed south-central and eastern regions of Spain on Friday, unleashing powerful torrents that swept away cars and swamped homes.

Madrigueras, located 120 miles northwest of Alicante, was the worst affected and was battered by a deluge that dumped 140 litres of rain in just three hours.

Rescuers found a 102-year-old woman lifeless inside her home, which was swallowed by more than three feet of floodwater.



Astonishing footage and photos showed the carnage caused by the freak weather, with cars piled up on top of each other in the centre of the town.

Desperate locals were seen trapped on balconies watching cars sweep away, with one man filmed clinging to his vehicle to avoid being dragged away by the powerful floodwaters.

The sheer force of the downpour left streets completely submerged, flooded homes and businesses and cut several major access routes into the town.

Officials fear similar scenes could strike Barcelona in the coming hours.



Heavy rain and storms also affected parts of the Costa Blanca last night where orange and yellow alerts were in place.

On Friday, Valencia shut down schools for nearly half a million children while Catalonia has put three towns into lockdown.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is understood the extreme weather was triggered by cold gusts that collided with humid air hanging low over the Meditterarnean sea, triggering slow-moving but violent thunderstorms all along Spain‘s eastern coastline.

The devastating weather pattern – known as Dana – often occurs in autumn.

News.title: Man, 47, found ‘shot in the head’ in UK van carrying 10 illegal migrants at rest stop on French motorway
News.content:
'SHOOTING' MYSTERY Man, 47, found ‘shot in the head’ in UK van carrying 10 illegal migrants at rest stop on French motorway







Next

A MAN has been found shot dead inside a Brit tradesman’s van carrying ten illegal migrants at a French motorway rest stop.

The vehicle was found at a stop around 20 miles north of the city of Troyes and 200 miles away from the Channel crossing.



The body of a 47-year-old man was found with a “gunshot wound to his head” inside the van at around 5am on Friday.

A suspect “believed to have been present at the crime scene” was arrested after the shocking discovery, Troyes prosecutor Isabelle Verissimo said.



The van had UK licence plates, however the driver’s nationality has not yet been revealed.

Cops also found “around 10 foreign nationals who were irregularly on French territory,” inside the vehicle.

An initial investigation suggested that shots were fired into the van as it stopped to park at the Champ l’Epée rest stop.

Several people then fled the scene, according to Verissimo.

She said that a criminal investigation would be opened today for murder, attempted murder, and unauthorised possession of a weapon.

The probe will also look into “aiding the irregular entry, the movement and the residence of a foreigner in France as part of an organised group, and human trafficking as part of an organised group”.



The A26 motorway runs over 220 miles, from Troyes to Calais and is known in France as the “motorway of the English” (Autoroute des Anglais) because it is always full of people travelling to and from Britain.

Last year, the RAID – an elite French special forces unit – was involved in a deadly shoot-out with Iraqi-Kurd pople smugglers at a motorway service rest area on the A31, near Dijon.

It emerged at the time that Karzan Ghazi Kareem, 39, was blasted to death during the gun fight in February 2025.

His brother, 45-year-old Idriss Ghazi Kareem was an English Channel migrant “super smuggler” who organised small boat crossings worth £50million a year from prison, investigators revealed.

Idriss Ghazi Kareem is currently serving a 15-year sentence for the manslaughter of seven Afghans who drowned on the way to the UK.

News.title: Burnham blasted for ‘dereliction of duty’ by Shadow Chancellor as he warns cost of living is in ‘nosebleed territory’
News.content:
Next

ANDREW Griffith has warned that Britain’s economy is “in peril right now” and Andy Burnham has no plan to fix it.

The Tory Shadow Chancellor said the cost of living crisis is in “nosebleed territory” with diesel prices and energy bills soaring.



Meanwhile, business chiefs are packing their backs and fleeing Britain because they are fed up with Labour’s tax raids.

He accused the Prime Minister of a “dereliction of duty” for failing to address this urgent crisis and instead doling out election promises for 2030.



Mr Griffith said: “The country is in peril right now.

“Defence is unfunded right now. We are paying the highest borrowing rates in 28 years right now.

“The welfare budget for working age people is out of control right now.

“The dereliction of duty that we heard last week was talking about vibes in 2030 and beyond when we have a homegrown crisis right here, right now.”

Mr Burnham used the Labour’s Party conference in Liverpool to set out his policy pledges for the next election, pencilled in for 2029.

He said he would fix the social care crisis by watering down the pensions triple lock, introduce a PR electoral system, and opened the door to reversing Brexit.



Trashing his predecessors, the Labour PM also vowed to “break with the direction of the past 40 years”.

Speaking to The Sun on Sunday on the eve of the Tory Party’s own conference in Birmingham, Mr Griffith said the PM is stuck in a time warp.

He said: “I was quite shocked to hear Andy Burnham paint a vision of taking us back to a 1970s that never really existed.

“The idea that the thing that’s wrong with Britain today is that we don’t have enough public ownership, not enough regulations, and that taxes aren’t high enough.

I was genuinely shocked by that.”



He added: “Young people don’t want to go back to the 1970s. They want to go forward to the 2040s.”

Britain’s economy is stuck in the slow lane while bills are soaring – and expected to get worse because of the Iran War.

Mr Griffith said the Labour PM woefully failed to say how he would address this crisis, harking back to old debates about the EU.

He slammed Mr Burnham for suggesting the UK could reverse Brexit.



“It would be a catastrophe to take us back to the divisive debates around Brexit, and to try and tie us back into a body of European regulations, when that is not a fast-growing part of the global economy”, Mr Griffith said.

“And it would be a colossal betrayal of the 2016 vote.”

He is equally damning about Labour’s vow to introduce PR voting, accusing the PM of “trying to rig the very system of democracy we operate in”.

He said: “The prospect of a red, yellow, green, rainbow coalition rightly fills me with horror.

“You’d have the worst of every party: higher energy bills, higher taxes, more pettifogging regulation from Whitehall to the town hall.”



But quizzed on the PM’s pledge to fix social care by watering down the pensions triple lock, Mr Griffith is less clear.

He said the Tories are committed to the pensions triple lock for this parliament – but refused to say they would fight the next election on a promise to keep it.

Mr Griffith said: “We are committed to the triple lock for this Parliament. That was in our manifesto. Kemi Badenoch and I absolutely stand by that.”

Pressed on if the triple lock will be in their next manifesto, he said: “We will tell you all about our exciting plans at the next election.”



Although Mr Griffith said pensioners who have paid their taxes deserve “dignity in retirement” and that his focus is on cutting benefits for people who can but won’t work.

Britain is on course to spend a staggering £100 billion on sickness and disability benefits by 2030 – more than the entire defence budget.

Nearly 1 million 18 to 24 year-olds are not in work or training – dubbed NEETs. This is one of the highest rates in the Western world.

Taking aim at the broken welfare system, Mr Griffith said: “I think it’s widely accepted that we have a welfare bill that is out of control.

“It’s putting strain on the public finances to the extent we have a prime minister who talks about prioritising social security over national security.



“The government is scrabbling around for the £10 billion per year finance funding for defense that its own independent review called for. And it’s unable to find that money.

“Our plans are firm but fair. That young people should not leave education and go onto a life of welfare.”

The Tories have announced plans to ban welfare claimants using their benefits to buy booze and new rules forcing under-25s to look for work to qualify for payments.

They are expected to announce more policies cracking down on welfare at their conference this week.

Mr Griffith said he is “very happy as Chancellor being respected but not popular” when it comes to curbing barmy handouts – like free cars for people with ADHD.



For the shadow chancellor, turning the UK economy around and tackling the bloated benefits bill go hand in hand.

He said Labour’s new workers rights laws and tax rises have put bosses off hiring – fuelling the NEETs crisis and harming growth.

These new rules and regulations are “chilling the heart of every employer” and killing the Saturday job, he warned.

The Tory Treasury chief is also worried that so many business chiefs and investors are leaving Britain for other countries.

Hedge fund billionaire Chris Rokos, the UK’s third largest taxpayer, has recently announced he is moving to Greece.



Mr Griffith said: “The Prime Minister talks of growth in every postcode. Who knew he meant postcodes in Athens, Paris and Milan.”

But his biggest concern is the cost of living crisis. As we speak in a wood-pannelled office in Parliament, diesel prices have soared to £2 a litre – their highest in history.

Mr Griffith said: “Its nosebleed territory. We would not be putting up fuel duty – something the government is planning to do at the end of the year.”

Drawing a clear blue line between the Tories and Labour, Mr Griffith said he will be a “tax-cutting chancellor”.



The Tories are expected to use their conference to announce plans to abolish inheritance tax, a massive policy pledge exclusively revealed in The Sun on Sunday last month.

Mr Griffith said: “This country, the economy, cannot hope to grow with the current record level of tax burden. It’s that simple.

“The path to do that responsibly is by cutting the leviathan of government spending: the out of control welfare, the size of government itself, and the waste of money on things like overseas aid.”

The Conservative Party has gone through a tough time recently.

They suffered the worst general election defeat in history in 2024 and have spent much of the two years since trailing Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party in the polls.



There are some signs that under Kemi Badenoch’s leadership the Tories are starting to recover some support.

But it is early days, and the Tories still need to prove they can be trusted on the economy and immigration.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Griffith sees his role as convincing former Tory voters the party is “safe to come home to”.

He said: “This is the party of Kemi Badenoch, but also of Margaret Thatcher and Winston Churchill – and we are not going anywhere.”

News.title: Teen, 15, riding unregistered bike left fighting for life after crash with car
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CRASH HORROR Teen, 15, riding unregistered bike left fighting for life after crash with car







Next

A TEENAGER riding an unregistered bike has been left fighting for his life after a crash involving a car.

The horror unfolded at around 5.20pm on Thursday in the Holme Wood area of Bradford, West Yorkshire.

Cops said the collision involved a black Audi S3 and an unregistered electric motorcycle on School Street.



The rider of the motorcycle – a 15-year-old boy – was raced to hospital after sustaining a serious head injury.



His current condition is described as “critical”.

A spokesperson for West Yorkshire Police said: “The Roads Policing Unit is investigating this matter, and is urging anyone who witnessed the collision, or who saw the movements of either vehicle prior to it, to contact them.

“Anyone with footage which may assist this investigation is also asked to make contact.”



Any witnesses are urged to contact the Roads Policing Unit quoting reference 1259 of October 1.

News.title: Tories unveil their own Bayeux Tapestry which includes the notoroious photo of vaping Angela Rayner in a dinghy
News.content:
The Tories are unveiling their own spoof version of the Bayeux Tapestry, which immortalises the famous Sun on Sunday frontpage

ON ME THREAD Tories unveil their own Bayeux Tapestry which includes the notoroious photo of vaping Angela Rayner in a dinghy







Next

THE SUN on Sunday has been honoured in the Tory Party’s spoof version of the Bayeux Tapestry.

The Conservatives will unveil their 88-foot take on the historic woven artwork at their party conference in Birmingham this week.



It pokes fun at the Labour government’s trials and tribulations, including Sir Keir Starmer’s downfall and the rise of new PM Andy Burnham.

One eye-catching panel immortalises The Sun on Sunday’s front page picture of Angela Rayner vaping on an inflatable dinghy – as we revealed she had bought a third home for nearly £800,000.



The award-winning scoop helped trigger Ms Rayner’s resignation as deputy PM as it emerged she had failed to pay nearly £40,000 in stamp duty.

Another panel shows The Sun on Sunday’s Political Editor Kate Ferguson writing in her reporter’s notebook as Sir Keir lets prisoners out of jail early and Rachel Reeves hand out bags of gold to trade union barons.

The Tory tableau is inspired by the Bayeux Tapestry, which was handwoven 950 years ago and tells the story of events leading up to the Norman Conquest of 1066.

It is currently on display in Britain for the first time in over 900 years – at the British Museum – where it is a smash hit.

The Tory version has been months in the planning and uses a combination of human designers and AI.



It is printed on cloth and is expected to be the star attraction at the conference this year.

Even Labour insiders were impressed by the tapestry, with one telling The Sun on Sunday: “Fair play – it’s a brilliant idea.”

News.title: Cornell 7 frat bros shared photo of alleged victim on Snapchat before ‘repeatedly raping her in closet’
News.content:
Next

MEMBERS of the Chi Phi fraternity at the center of the Cornell University gang rape case reportedly sent a photo of the alleged victim before she says they attacked her.

The former student, identified only as Jane Doe, was allegedly subjected to a horrifying hours-long gang rape at the squalid Chi Phi fraternity house on October 25, 2024, according to court docs.



She alleged in a civil lawsuit that when she was 20 years old, she was drugged and raped by seven fellow Cornell students who allegedly sent sick messages in a Snapchat group chat inviting pals to have sex with her.

Part of this messaging thread in the Chi Phi Actives group with over 50 members included one man saying, “Like you can walk in and whip it out.”



Court papers say a message was posted at about 1:42 am in the group that read, “Free p***y“.

Doe claims that multiple men entered the bedroom she was in and the assaults continued until around 5:45am.

read more on Cornell 7 DEN OF FILTH Haunting new pics from Cornell 7 room where woman was 'drugged & gang raped'



According to social media images obtained by CBS News, fraternity members shared a photo of her in the Snapchat group on the night of the alleged attack.

The photo, obtained by the news outlet via Doe’s attorney, appears to show her smiling with another man.

It was directly after this photo was sent that one member in the chat asked, “Shop still open?” before being told “Yes”.

“This is crazy work,” another message reads.



In May 2025, seven months after the alleged assaults, Doe said at a university hearing that she “felt like bait” and “was a sex doll for all intents and purposes,” per the university’s IX investigation.

“I felt like lions around me. It was a totally debilitating place to be in.”

She told investigators that at some point during the horror attack, she was taken into a closet by two of the men.

“It was just raping,” she said, adding that she was drifting in and out of consciousness during the repeated assaults.

Doe says three of the men apologized to her three days after, by which point she says she had already collected evidence, including the dress she wore that night, and gone to a clinic for a urinary tract infection.



According to the lawsuit, she told doctors that she contracted the infection in a “traumatic way,” at which point she was told to “speak with somebody” rather than be offered a rape kit.

On November 7, she took a rape kit test after realizing the full scope of what allegedly transpired, and went to campus police the following day.

No arrests have been made or criminal charges filed in relation to the alleged attack.

The case was reopened last month, and New York Governor Kathy Hochul has now appointed Attorney General Letitia James as prosecutor in the case after “losing faith” in the original investigators who declined to file charges.

Matthew Van Houten, the Tompkins County district attorney, defended his office’s decision not to file charges, saying they never saw a transcript of a conversation between Jane and campus police where she said she was raped.



The district attorney said the original statement did not allege that Jane had unknowingly been drugged or that she had been forced into sexual acts.

“She never says that she was drugged without her knowledge,” Van Houten said.

“She admits to taking drugs and alcohol voluntarily and with knowledge.”



However, in her initial multi-day interviews with campus police, Jane explicitly told investigators, “I can say with 100% confidence I was raped.”

It remains unclear who omitted the phrase from the executive summaries forwarded by campus police to the Tompkins County District Attorney’s office.

Van Houten has also acknowledged that his office had not previously been given the Snapchat image that now forms part of the lawsuit.

Cornell supports the decision to reopen the criminal investigation.

All seven fraternity members named in the lawsuit by Jane Doe have denied the allegations against them.



The U.S. Sun is naming only the men who have publicly responded to the allegations or had attorneys issue statements for them.

Scott Kretzschmar, Scott Norris and Gillio Lopes have all denied wrongdoing through public statements or their lawyers.

The Cornell 7 case, which has made headlines across the globe, is now an active criminal investigation, and prosecution will be pursued if warranted, officials said.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call RAINN (Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network) at 800-656-HOPE (4673).

News.title: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford released on bail
News.content:
A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on bail.

The 25-year-old man was arrested in the London borough of Westminster on Thursday. Searches of two properties in the same area have now finished.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire last weekend.

Five other men in their twenties were arrested and were subsequently released on police bail. All five were UK nationals from London.

The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the events are continuing, police said.

Last weekend, the five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF), sparking a major security incident.

The BBC understands that one of the men had dialled 999 himself, about an hour before a local farmer alerted police to a "large group" of masked men near the vehicles.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail on Monday in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting that afternoon in response. He later said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident, but did not provide any more details.

Tehran has strongly denied any involvement. The Iranian embassy in London said on Monday that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.

News.title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage
News.content:
The 2026 Conservative conference is big enough to justify using Birmingham's Symphony Hall as its main stage again.

So, Kemi Badenoch will tread the same stage ageing rockers Marillion took last month - and where sequinned soprano Katherine Jenkins will perform next week. She'll also avoid the humiliation of a national party leader being squashed into a side room at a corporate conference centre (with drapes portioning off the empty space). Simply, the party is able to put bums on seats again - and by that measure, things are looking up.

Badenoch goes into the conference with her own position secure in the party. One senior Tory says "she has actually defied cynics like me" who initially disapproved of her leadership. Her standing with the public has improved and she is now, again on a very simple but crucial measure, much better known. Her allies are sure she has developed a clear identity among the public, confiding: "People now know who she is and they enjoy her interventions - the thing we hear most is I don't always agree with her but I know where she stands."

News.title: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told
News.content:
Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb.

Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.

One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025.

Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October, when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London.

As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford.

The Metropolitan Police said the men were alleged to have obtained instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquired liquids and other components to make an improvised explosive device.

They are accused of using the internet to identify and research potential targets, acquiring images, plans and maps.

Prosecutor Mark Luckett told the court: "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device.

"The defendants were observed carrying out, what the prosecution say, is a hostile reconnaissance within Manchester's Jewish community, identifying attempted targets such as the Jewish Museum and Heaton Park Synagogue."

News.title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?
News.content:
Months before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.

You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view.

When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.

But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.

Last week, US pop star Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled tour, and surprises from the show, which scores of fans have paid a lot of money to see, have already been dissected online.

Tours by Harry Styles, Charli XCX and Ariana Grande have also been filmed from every angle and shared over the past few months.

While some fans lap up the opportunity to see what's coming, others are taking extreme measures to preserve the element of surprise.

News.title: EV drivers love their cars, but some passengers feel sick - this could be why
News.content:
Lola Baird has just asked her boyfriend to pull over. Forty minutes into a journey and she's feeling "overwhelmed" by nausea - and can't stop herself throwing up on the ground next to his car.

Lola, 24, from north London, had never experienced motion sickness until her boyfriend bought an electric vehicle (EV) two years ago. Ever since, she's been feeling "very nauseous" when he takes her on long car journeys.

It's become so severe she's even asked him to change his car.

Lola isn't alone. Other people told BBC News that they or their children notice feeling more car sick when sitting as a passenger in an electric vehicle. But at the same time, many EV drivers say it's not been a concern.

So what could explain these reports of motion sickness?

Dr Irene Di Giulio, senior lecturer in anatomy and biomechanics at King's College London whose research includes motion sickness, says research so far suggests some people experience more severe motion sickness in electric vehicles than in non-electric vehicles.

It's something Dr Nicholas Hac, a neurologist at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago who specialises in dizziness and vertigo, has also heard from some of his patients. "They just notice that they're much more likely or prone to be motion sick" in electric vehicles, he says.

"I've heard about it many, many, many times," he adds, saying about two patients a month specifically reference feeling motion sick in electric vehicles.

News.title: Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.

As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.

Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment.

"It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day.

"But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."

The episode drew in a peak audience of 8.6 million viewers, just short of the debut episode with an average of 8.9 million viewers.

The morning following Rajan's banishment, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."

Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.

The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.

News.title: Why thousands of couples are choosing Scotland to say 'I do'
News.content:
Hayden Kuhn and Savannah Aanderud had never set foot in Scotland before they decided it was the perfect place to get married last May.

The couple, from Pennsylvania in the US, wanted a destination wedding that would take their family and friends on an adventure with them.

They considered locations across Europe, before deciding on Scotland after Savannah saw photographs of a castle wedding online.

"I think it was on Pinterest," she said. "Somebody got married in a castle and I was like 'Oh, I have to do that'."

The pair are far from alone in seeing Scotland as the ultimate romantic destination.

News.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
News.content:
"It felt very real to me. I'm really new to panic attacks, so I need to learn more about it," she added.

The Birmingham-born presenter, who also co-hosts The Great British Bake Off, thanked NHS staff and her colleagues at This Morning, including O'Leary.

"It's really warmed my heart actually. I didn't necessarily want to be on the news or anything like that but this is a new world to me," she said.

"I'm going to take stock, take some rest and I'll see you soon."

Friday's edition of the ITV show began at 10:00 BST with Hammond and her regular co-host O'Leary at the helm, before she left at 11:30 during a segment about pets.

O'Leary, 53, addressed her absence when the show returned from a break, saying: "Welcome back to This Morning, Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she's just had to duck out. Hopefully she'll be back."

He later updated viewers that she would, in fact, not be returning, "so I'll be here for the rest of the show".

Hammond rose to fame as contestant on Channel 4 reality show Big Brother before appearing on I'm A Celebrity and Strictly Come Dancing.

She became a co-host in This Morning in 2021, and was part of the team that won a National Television Award for best daytime programme the following year.

She joined Bake Off in 2023 and took over from the late Paul O'Grady on For the Love of Dogs in 2024.

News.title: Man shot dead as families gather for memorial
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people â including children â gathered for a memorial service in west London.

The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.

Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.

No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.

Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence.

"We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated.

"We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."

He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw".

He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?

"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media.

"However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."

News.title: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s
News.content:
Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Green Party.

Announcing the policy at the party's conference in Brighton, co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said there were a million "bored, desperate and lost" young people who were out of work, training or education.

Under the proposed scheme, youngsters would be offered posts in the private sector, with the government paying half their salary.

Ali said an initial pilot scheme - rolled out in areas with the fewest job openings for young people - would create 9,000 jobs, at an overall cost of Â£110m.

The pilot would start in areas such as Rotherham, Ceredigion, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Broxtowe and South Staffordshire, with an ambition to roll it out nationwide.

The party said that a person not in work, education or training would cost the state an estimated Â£240,000 in benefits over the course of their lifetime.

It argued that its policy would reduce spending on welfare and boost tax receipts from employment.

Employers would be exempt from paying National Insurance contributions, but would have to provide in-job training, the party says.

The party is seeking to pitch the plan as more ambitious than the government's own scheme, which subsidises six-month job placements for benefit claimants who have been looking for work for 18 months.

Ali also criticised ministers for previously suggesting youngsters refusing a role under that scheme could lose access to benefits, telling activists: "Threatening young people with cuts to Universal Credit if they don't accept short-term work placements - that's not a youth strategy."

Speaking to BBC News after his speech, Ali said: "If we don't take action now, we're losing a generation of young people."

The number of 16-24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training has been rising since the Covid pandemic, with figures reaching almost one million.

A long-awaited report into the problem by former Labour minister Alan Milburn is expected to be published this autumn.

News.title: Huge crowds turn out in support of residents over Drumcree parade dispute
News.content:
Rallies are being held in Portadown on both sides of the Drumcree parade dispute as the stand-off between Garvaghy Road residents and the Orange Order continues.

Addressing thousands of people at an event on the Garvaghy Road, First Minister and Sinn FÃ©in vice president Michelle O'Neill said she heard the Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant "talk about being between a rock and a hard place", adding she has "never heard such nonsense, this is between right and wrong".

The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) said anyone blocking the Garvaghy Road will be "treated as participating in an unnotified and therefore illegal protest and that anyone "found to have broken the law will face criminal justice consequences".

Speaking at Drumcree church, Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) MP Carla Lockhart repeated calls for PSNI Chief Constable Jon Boutcher and his officers to "do their job" and facilitate the parade, describing the current impasse as "mob rule".

For most of the afternoon stewards in high visibility jackets kept people off the Garvaghy Road and those attending were told it was important to allow traffic to flow freely.

However, by 15:00 BST the crowd was so large that they were standing on the road as police closed it to traffic.

The fallout over the proposed Orange Order march - which is opposed by residents of the Garvaghy Road - has lasted since Sunday morning after the Parades Commission's decision that the Orange Order parade could go ahead with restrictions.

News.title: Police appeal to help find heavily pregnant woman
News.content:
Police have appealed for help in their search for a missing woman who is heavily pregnant.

Leicestershire Police said Charlie Ryan was reported missing on Friday morning, having last been seen in the Groby Road area of Leicester near to New Parks Way roundabout.

The force said the 31-year-old is white, 165cm (5ft 5in), with bright blonde hair. She was last seen wearing a black jacket, grey jumper, black leggings and black shoes.

Officers said they were "extremely concerned" for her welfare and active inquiries were continuing to find her.

Police said inquiries carried out so far indicated she may be in the Northfields area of Leicester.

Anyone who may have seen her or knows where she may be is asked to contact police.

News.title: Watch the moment a landslip leaves Skye drivers facing a 40-mile diversion
News.content:
Drivers on Skye are facing a 40-mile diversion after a landslide led to a road closure.

The ground fell away from the side of the A855 north of Uig onto a local access road on Friday afternoon and an inspection later confirmed it would have to stay shut over the weekend.

The A855 road encircles the Trotternish peninsula in the north of the island and a diversion route is now in place.

No-one was injured by the landslip - which was caught on CCTV from a nearby house - but a group of visiting schoolchildren found themselves temporarily separated from their packed lunches until a local woman volunteered to retrieve them by bike.

The road could have to remain closed into next week as "detailed surveying" works continue, according to local councillor Chrissie Gillies.

News.title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
News.content:
The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.

The party said it would cost Â£2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.

On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.

Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.

Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.

Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.

Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.

The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.

The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.

An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

News.title: Youth charged after shopping centre attack leaves teenager in hospital
News.content:
A teenager has been charged after an attack involving a groups of youths inside a Glasgow shopping centre left another teenager needing hospital treatment.

Video posted on social media shows a young man, who was using a crutch and wearing a medical boot, being knocked to the ground, then repeatedly punched and kicked inside the St Enoch Centre on Friday afternoon.

A second person was also pushed to the ground during the disturbance but security staff intervened.

Police Scotland said a 19-year-old was taken to hospital and a 17-year-old boy was later arrested and charged following investigations.

The attackers had run off by the time officers arrived and the injured man, who was bleeding from a head wound, was initially helped by shoppers and security staff.

News.title: Suppliers pile pressure on government over energy bills
News.content:
The government should take immediate action to help those struggling with energy bills this winter, the suppliers' trade body has said.

Energy UK said domestic gas prices, which rose on Thursday, and forecasts of steep rises in January meant inaction would lead to a longer-term, more costly and deeper crisis.

Figures revealed by the BBC earlier this week showed forecasters predicting a 16% rise in domestic energy prices in the new year for 20 million households on variable tariffs affected by regulator Ofgem's price cap.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the government was considering any measure that took the pressure off.

Households in England, Scotland and Wales on variable energy tariffs set by Ofgem's price cap, which puts a maximum price on each unit of gas and electricity, were hit with a 4% price increase at the start of October.

That is the equivalent of about Â£60 per year - or Â£5 per month - taking an annual bill to Â£1,723 for the typical household using both electricity and gas and paying by direct debit if this level was sustained for a year.

But forecasts show a far greater increase is possible for bills in January. Consultancy Cornwall Insight said its latest forecast suggested the same typical annual bill would rise to Â£1,999.

A New York district attorney declined to review additional evidence gathered by Cornell University police before deciding not to pursue criminal charges in a gang rape investigation, according to newly obtained records.

The records, obtained by the New York Times, show that on November 25, 2024, a Cornell investigator told a member of the Tompkins County district attorney’s office that campus police had conducted additional interviews. Prosecutors did not ask to review the evidence and instead agreed that, based on a six-page statement from the former student known as Jane Doe, “criminal charges would not be pursued in this case.”

But before prosecutors declined to pursue charges, Cornell police had conducted interviews, reviewed messages, logged tips and contacted people connected to the case. The investigation continued through January 2025, but prosecutors did not review the additional evidence, a decision not previously reported, according to The Times.

The case stems from a civil lawsuit filed last month by Jane Doe, who alleges she was drugged and gang-raped by seven Chi Phi fraternity members in October 2024. All of the men have denied wrongdoing, and none has been criminally charged. New York officials are now reviewing the case in light of the civil lawsuit.

A spokesperson for the Tompkins County D.A.’s Office pushed back on The Times’ report in a statement to The Independent Saturday, saying: “The ‘interviews’ being cited were essentially each of the seven suspects telling the police that they would not speak to them on the advice of counsel.”

open image in gallery Newly obtained documents say the DA declined to review additional evidence in the Cornell rape investigation, while the office tells The Independent that the cited interviews were simply suspects refusing to speak on their lawyers’ advice ( AFP/Getty )

After the civil lawsuit, there was strong reaction from many questioning why the fraternity members weren’t charged, raising questions about rape on the nation’s college campuses and whether Cornell officials handled it properly.

The handling of the case is now under renewed scrutiny and criticism that has made national headlines. On Friday, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul criticized Cornell police and the district attorney before appointing Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor with the authority to bring criminal charges.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten reportedly told The Times Thursday that additional records gathered by Cornell police were “not pertinent to our analysis because we had Jane Doe’s comprehensive account of the events.”

Van Houten has defended his decision not to prosecute, saying Jane Doe’s police statement “described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious and consensual.” The statement did not establish a crime under New York law, he claimed.

Former prosecutors and legal experts have questioned the decision to rely primarily on the campus police investigation.

“We would never rely on a campus police investigation,” Rick Trunfio, a former upstate New York sex crimes prosecutor and Syracuse University law professor, told The Times. “There are too many problems with that.”

Trunfio said the case should have been handled by a specialized police or prosecution team.

“You think Cornell University wants to report something like that?” he added.

A Cornell representative who speaks for campus police declined The Times’ request for comment, citing pending litigation.

The Independent has contacted Cornell for comment.

For the first time, all 15 of the couples will have the chance to perform a routine inspired by a cinema classic as they battle it out to survive the first elimination.

The show will kick off with a Zootropolis-inspired performance from the Strictly pros, before the celebrities take to the dance floor with routines inspired by Toy Story, Beauty and the Beast, Wicked: For Good, Mary Poppins, and The Greatest Showman.

As the countdown begins for this week’s show, here’s everything you need to know...

England will bid to again banish the noise as they take on Croatia in the Nations League amid the fallout from the Manchester City verdict.

One might have forgiven a few in Thomas Tuchel’s squad for being a little distracted after a seismic moment for the sport, but England produced a professional enough performance against the Czech Republic on Tuesday to secure a 2-0 win. It felt a quietly significant result for a manager still under pressure given the manner of his side’s World Cup exit, and Tuchel will be hopeful of another strong showing on another tough away day.

England beat Croatia in their World Cup opener earlier in the year, though the hosts have re-appointed Slaven Bilic since the end of that tournament. Though no match for world champions Spain in their last outing, there is plenty of experience and quality in the home ranks – though only schoolchildren in the stands due to crowd restrictions after disturbances from Croatian fans in Paris last year.

A “special guest” will reportedly join Ed Sheeran’s beleaguered U.S. tour in Atlanta tonight after all of his support acts withdrew over the Macklemore saga.

In an Instagram post, Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta shared a graphic with information for attendees ahead of Saturday night’s show, stating that “special guest takes the stage at 7 p.m,” while Sheeran will perform an hour later at 8 p.m. The Independent has contacted Sheeran’s representatives for comment.

Last month, all of Sheeran’s support acts scheduled for his U.S. dates — including Irish singer Aaron Rowe and American producer Finneas — withdrew from the tour in solidarity with Macklemore, who was removed from the tour last month over his “Free Palestine” remarks onstage in New Jersey.

Sheeran had responded to calls from Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft, who had said the rapper could not perform at his venue after his public pro-Palestine comments.

At the time, Sheeran said he would not be drawn into public debate about the war in Gaza but insisted he was “not complicit.” The singer faced significant scrutiny for his apolitical image, and protesters gathered outside Sheeran’s first concert without Macklemore on September 19.

open image in gallery A “special guest” will reportedly join Ed Sheeran’s beleaguered U.S. tour in Atlanta tonight, according to the venue ( Instagram via @mercedesbenzstadium )

The controversy has sparked something of a movement in the music industry. On Friday night, country musician Zach Bryan wore a “Free Palestine” shirt during his concert at Kraft’s stadium in Massachusetts.

His guitarist, Noah Le Gros, wore a Palestine soccer jersey onstage alongside Bryan, and later shared a picture of himself in the shirt standing in front of a Kraft Sports and Entertainment sign at the Massachusetts stadium.

open image in gallery Ed Sheeran has performed his last three concerts on his beleaguered tour without support acts ( AFP/Getty )

Last week, Macklemore responded to being dropped from Sheeran’s tour by announcing a “Free Palestine” tour with unannounced special guests, with proceeds from the shows in Paris, London and Dublin going to organizations supporting Palestinians.

Sheeran addressed the fallout onstage at a solo concert at Lincoln Financial Field on September 19, and said he was “so sorry” for disappointing his fans.

“I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division; about humanity, not politics,” he said.

He clarified his own stance on the Israel-Palestine conflict, saying, “What happened in Israel, and at the music festival on October 7th, was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate.”

President Donald Trump appeared to share the personal phone number of a senator in his push to make daylight saving time permanent.

The president is putting pressure on Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas to support a bill to make the move permanent. He urged people to call what appeared to be the personal cellphone number of Cotton, the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee.

The Sunshine Protection Act passed the House in July, but it faces roadblocks in the Senate where some Republicans are strongly opposed.

Proponents, including the White House, argue that the change would provide more daylight during the times that Americans are most active. Detractors said permanent daylight saving time would lead to darker and potentially more hazardous winter mornings when children will be waiting for school buses and parents will be driving to work in darkness.

Daylight saving time is that period between spring and fall when clocks in most parts of the United States are set one hour ahead of standard time. Not all states observe it — and under the bill, states can opt out of the change if their respective legislatures act to do so before the bill's enactment.

"For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill and, in the Senate, it's very easy to do, it only takes one!" Trump wrote on social media, noting that passing the bill would give professional golfers more time on the greens. "So, everyone in Arkansas, a State I love, and won 3 times, the last by by 34 points, tell Tom to, GET IT DONE! It will be appreciated by all," Trump said.

Trump included a phone number with an Arkansas area code.

open image in gallery John Thune, the Republican senate leader, is opposed to the bill to make daylight savings permanent ( AFP/Getty )

This is not the first time Trump has released personal information about a senator. While competing for the 2016 Republican presidential nomination, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina described Trump as "unfit for office" after Trump denigrated the military service of Sen. John McCain of Arizona. Trump then released Graham's personal cellphone number. That prompted a viral video in which the senator dramatically destroyed a series of flip phones. Graham later became a close ally of Trump.

Cotton, a member of Republican leadership, reiterated his opposition to permanent daylight saving time in a social media post of his own. Saturday afternoon, though he is not the only Republican who opposes it.

"No one likes changing the clock, me included, but Congress has enacted permanent Daylight Savings Time multiple times before and repealed it each time once Americans experienced absurdly late sunrises in the winter," he wrote. "Arkansans don't want their kids going to school in the pitch dark, and I'll always put Arkansas first."

A 2025 poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research shows that if forced to choose, most Americans would prefer to keep that extra hour of daylight in the evening. Only 12% of U.S. adults favor the current system of daylight saving time, which requires people in most states to change clocks twice a year, while 47% are opposed and 40% are neutral.

Members of Congress have long been interested in the potential benefits and costs of daylight saving time since it was first adopted as a wartime measure in 1942. The Senate passed a bill four years ago to make daylight saving time permanent, but it stalled in the House.

Trump’s Truth Social post in full:

Everybody in Arkansas, Tom Cotton, a friend of mine, is holding up a very important Bill. It’s called, “The Sunshine Protection Act” or, “We Don’t Want to Change Our Clocks Twice a Year Act.” For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill and, in the Senate, it’s very easy to do, it only takes one! It should pass overwhelmingly, in a Bipartisan fashion. So, everyone in Arkansas, a State I love, and won 3 times, the last by by 34 points, tell Tom to, GET IT DONE! It will be appreciated by all. Nobody wants to spend their precious time running all over the place, turning Clocks back twice a year and, having sunshine in the afternoon is better than early in the morning! The PGA TOUR, as an example, needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments. Likewise, regular Golfers, Tennis Players, Hunters and, perhaps most importantly, Farmers who want more Daylight to play or work. See letter from Brian Rolapp, CEO of the PGA TOUR below. 65% PLUS want more sun in the afternoon, Daylight Saving Time (The way it is now!), but 100% don’t want to change their Clocks twice a year. They want to, as they say, “LOCK THE CLOCK!” Who doesn’t? It’s very expensive for our Nation where you have high and dangerous steeples to reach, like on churches and municipal buildings. Almost everybody wants “The Sunshine Protection Act” to pass, except for Tom Cotton. To the Great People of Arkansas, please let your Senator know it would be a GREAT Bipartisan WIN for the United States Senate, and for America, itself. Call Tom on his cellphone at, 479-453-0533, and let him know. “The Sunshine Protection Act” was passed in the House by a Vote of 308 to 117. HAVE THE SENATE VOTE, NOW! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

Police in Indiana have made an arrest in a decades-old cold case involving the deaths of a young boy and his stepmother.

Michael Jerome James, 35, has been indicted by a grand jury for allegedly murdering both Chynna Dickus and her stepson, Blake Dickus, according to the Franklin Police Department.

On July 24, 2006, Sean Dickus returned to his home and found the bodies of his 10-year-old son, Blake, and his wife, 26-year-old Chynna, according to Fox 59.

Over the 20 years that the case went unsolved — billboards and posters were put up offering $25,000 rewards for information that led to an arrest.

Then, last month, the billboards began offering more. Beginning in September, the reward for information leading to an arrest rose to $100,000. It seems that did the trick.

open image in gallery Michael Jerome James, 35, has been charged with the murders of Chynna Dickus and her 10-year-old stepson, Blake Dickus ( Johnson County Prosecutor's Office )

Now, police believe they have a suspect.

“For 20 years, Blake and Chynna’s families have carried the weight of an unimaginable loss waiting for this day,” a statement from the FPD said. “On behalf of the Franklin Police Department, I want them to know that we have never forgotten their loved ones, and we have never stopped seeking justice. Today’s development is an important moment, not only for our department, but most importantly for the families and Blake and Chynna whose lives were taken from them.”

FPD Police Chief Kirby Cochran said that investigators used forensic science and persistence to bring the case against James.

Grand jury members reviewed the evidence for three weeks before delivering the indictment.

Johnson County Prosecutor Lance D. Hamner said on Friday that the cold case motivated him to become a prosecutor.

“This tragic crime occurred during my first tenure as Johnson County Prosecutor in 2006, and the tragedy has remained with me ever since,” Hamner said. “In fact, a primary driving force behind my decision to leave the bench as judge and run for prosecutor once again was to seek justice in this case. This was something I could not talk about at the time.”

He said during the presser that his office cannot share further details about the evidence leading to James' arrest or the grand jury's deliberations at this time.

Casey Jarvis built on a fast start to make a fine seven-under par over the Old Course at St Andrews and take a two-stroke lead into the final round of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

The South African, who held a one-shot advantage overnight, had set off on the par-four 10th and opened with a superb eagle on his approach from 103 yards before also picking up three more birdies ahead of the turn despite the windy conditions.

Two more on the back nine, at three and five, saw him sign for a 65, to sit at 18 under, ahead of Englishman Matthew Jordan and Poland’s Adrian Meronk, who shot the joint-best round of the day with a nine-under 63 at Kingsbarns.

“I just felt like I was in control of my game today. I was really solid tee-to-green, and luckily rolled in a couple putts,” said Jarvis, who is aiming to close out a third DP World Tour win this season.

“Every golfer dreams of taking a lead, playing the Old Course on Sunday. I got goosebumps right now just standing here.

“I just can’t wait for tomorrow. Even if I don’t win, to be taking the lead, I am just going to enjoy it as much as I can.”

Jarvis added in quotes on the DP Tour website: “Obviously I know I am going to be feeling pressure tomorrow. I have won twice this year, so I kind of know how to deal with it a little better.

“I still know I am going to feel first tee nerves and pressure throughout the day, but I am just going to try and manage it as much as I can.”

Jordan, meanwhile, is looking for his first DP World Tour win in his 183rd tournament.

The Royal Liverpool member, who claimed the 2017 St Andrews Links Trophy victory as an amateur, carded a bogey-free 66 during his third round at Kingsbarns.

“I want to be in the last few groups and I want to give myself a really good chance on Sunday,” said Jordan, who had opened the tournament with a 69 at St Andrews and an impressive seven-under 65 at Carnoustie. “That’s what I have done today, so let’s see what tomorrow brings.”

Belgian Thomas Detry is at 15-under after his seven-under at St Andrews, while Denmark’s Jacob Skov Olesen made a nine-under 63 at Kingsbarns and is four shots off the lead alongside compatriot Niklas Norgaard, who played the Old Course in 67.

Jose Luis Ballester holed a 130-foot putt on the par-five fifth at St Andrews on his way to a four-under round which leaves him in a three-way tie for eighth at 12-under, alongside Scotland’s Calum Hill – whose 65 round at Kingsbarns included two bogeys and a double bogey as well as an eagle.

Matt Fitzpatrick made six under on the Old Course to also sit at 12 under, as is defending champion Bob MacIntyre who went round St Andrews in 68, recovering from a double-bogey at the second.
