An investigation has been launched over the mystery of why baby whales are washing up dead on the coast of Argentina.

The country’s Patagonian coast has seen scores of the calf carcasses washing ashore around Peninsula Valdes, on the country’s Patagonian coast.

The area is a major breeding ground for southern right whales in Argentina’s Chubut province.

Hunted to the brink of extinction in the 19th and 20th centuries, the whales now gather in the peninsula’s sheltered waters to give birth and nurse their young.

“We're looking into the whale calf deaths based on 23 years of monitoring that we have of this same population. That's what allows us to say that this is an unusual event," said Marcela Uhart, a veterinarian with the One Health Institute at the University of California, Davis, who is leading the investigation as head of the Southern Right Whale Health Monitoring Program.

The leading hypothesis is that the whale calves are suffering infections from marine bacteria that can enter their bodies through injuries inflicted by kelp gulls, Uhart said.

open image in gallery A dead southern right whale calf (Eubalaena australis) is removed by rangers using heavy machinery in Puerto Madryn, Chubut, Argentina on September 28, 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

For decades, the seabirds have pecked at whales surfacing to breathe, gorging on their skin and blubber. Adults learn to surface with only their heads exposed, keeping their backs underwater and out of reach of the gulls. Calves can't do that maneuver, leaving them vulnerable to attacks.

The carcasses have been washing ashore around the gulf city of Puerto Madryn, including near the central waterfront where they alarm residents and tourists. Residents have reported hundreds of them, but researchers declined to give a death toll, saying that would become clear after the season ends around late November.

Uhart and a team of biologists, veterinarians and park rangers have been searching the area for the dead calves from shore and with boats, planes and drones.

The work is gruesome: They photograph and examine the bodies, racing against decomposition to collect skin and organ samples for testing at a veterinary school farther north, in the city of Tandil. Bacteria have already been detected in those tissues, but researchers are still culturing samples to identify the microbes and determine whether infection was the cause of death, she said.

Even if bacteria are to blame, researchers must still determine why they have become so deadly this year.

open image in gallery Seabirds perch on the carcass of a southern right whale off El Doradillo Beach near Puerto Madryn, Argentina ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Changes in marine conditions like warming sea temperatures, potentially linked to climate change or El Nino, could contribute to “this perfect storm where this bacteria is powerful enough to overcome the immunity of the babies and cause their deaths,” Uhart said. “So to the extent that we can, we'll try to identify at least what factors may be triggering this event and making it so massive.”

Right whales got their name from whalers who considered them the “right” animals to hunt because they swam slowly, stayed close to shore and floated when killed, according to the International Whaling Commission, a global body tasked with regulating whaling.

Although illegal hunting continued into the 1970s, southern right whales have gradually rebounded since gaining international protection in 1935. But their recovery remains threatened by the same pressures facing whales worldwide: declining food supplies, fishing gear entanglements, oil spills and ship strikes.

If losses on this scale recur, they could slow the population’s recovery. By pinpointing what is killing the calves, researchers hope to find ways to protect the vulnerable population.

“If the cause relates to something that we are doing as humans, then we need to change that,” Uhart said. “We don’t want to endanger these whales again.”

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

News.title: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying
News.content:
The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

News.title: Bath complete revenge mission on Exeter despite imperious Feyi-Waboso
News.content:
Bath held off a furious comeback from Exeter, led by the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, to avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat here in June.

It felt as if lightning might strike Bath twice. Once again Exeter overturned a 26-10 half-time deficit, to manufacture a second-half lead thanks to a pair of blistering finishes by Feyi-Waboso. Four months ago, Bath failed to take a drop goal in the closing stages, but this time with the reassuring presence of Finn Russell at fly-half, they kept their cool.

The Scotland playmaker twice sent penalties deep into the Exeter 22 from where Stephen Varney conceded a yellow card and penalty try before Bath replacement Ted Hill powered through a thicket of Exeter tacklers.

“Finn is one of the best 10s in the world and I thought he had a very good game,” Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, said. “His decision making is above most players in the world and I thought that came through tonight.”

Despite the appearance of yet another high-scoring shoot-out, both teams defended with real bite, although Bath struggled to lay a finger on Feyi-Waboso who ended up in a scrap with a fan in the stands here when he was a spectator in May. He exacted a measure of revenge beating eight defenders and carried for 132 metres.

“Manny still needs game time,” Rob Baxter, the Exeter director of rugby, said. “When he’s on the ball, you see something incredible, but it is his ability to get on the ball again. He is just getting his game minutes and match fitness up.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

“This in turn has led to mounting financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, which has maintained upward pressure on the market interest rates which underpin mortgage pricing.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Polanski urges Miliband to block Rosebank oil field over Israel links | Green leader claims North Sea project is a test of Foreign Secretary’s proposed sanctions regime

2) Netherlands ditches wealth tax over exodus fears | Dutch PM scraps plan to target paper profits, instead introducing a more convention capital gains levy

3) Diesel crisis deepens as UK’s biggest refinery shuts for 10 weeks | Fears of squeeze on supplies after fuel costs rise higher than £2 per litre

4) Debt-ridden France branded ‘the new sick man of Europe’ | Investors hope the European Central Bank sees the struggling country as ‘too big to fail’

5) Britain blocks foreign lawyers after surge in south Asian applicants | Bar Standards Board halts scheme unless candidates have already secured a position

What happened overnight

The cost of government borrowing edged higher in Asia as soaring energy costs sparked inflation fears.

Bond yields, a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money, surged in September as investors brace for a period where interest rates stay higher for ​longer.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes hit 5.31pc, the ‌highest level since mid-June 2007. The 10-year yield gained 87 basis points in the July-September quarter, the biggest quarterly rise since 1994.

Market focus has been on how long US Treasury yields stay above the psychologically important 5pc level, while some investors even contemplate the possibility of yields breaching 6pc.

Yields in Japan have climbed to multi-decade highs too, while those in Germany, France and Britain have all hit 17 to 19 year peaks.

On Thursday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government ​bond yield was at 3.11pc, not far from the 30-year high it hit last week.

Asian technology stocks rose after a boost from AI chipmaker Micron, ​although US bonds struggled ‌after their sharpest quarterly sell-off in more than three decades as inflation risks from elevated energy prices linger.

Stalling peace talks between the US and Iran to end the seven-month-long war in the Middle East have kept crude prices aloft.Brent futures surged 42pc in the July-September quarter.

The high-stakes earnings from Micron, a key supplier to AI bellwether Nvidia, signalled strong demand for AI memory chips, with financial commitments under long-term supply agreements at $32 billion, up from $22 billion in June.

That helped push tech-heavy stock markets in Asia higher. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 3pc, and South Korea’s Kospi reversed earlier losses to gain 1.7pc. Taiwan’s stock benchmark was 0.8pc higher.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco, which is placed between the cheek and lower gum, is particularly popular in south Asia. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Eight tips for improving your laptop’s performance (and save your sanity)
News.content:
MacBooks and Windows laptops both have modes intended to maximise battery life. Low Power Mode (Mac) and Power Saver (Windows) should be avoided if you want peak performance.

On a Mac, you’ll find the Low Power Mode switch in Settings > Battery. For the best experience, set this to Never, but remember to change it back if you need your MacBook to last longer.

On a Windows laptop, there are two controls you need to consider. Both are found in Settings > System > Power & Battery.

Energy Saver mode uses multiple tactics to reduce battery consumption, including lowering maximum power. Switch this off, and you have access to Power Mode controls.

Your options are Best Power Efficiency, Balanced and Best Performance. While Balanced is the default, I was able to unlock up to 33 per cent more power by playing around with these settings using my own laptop.

To make matters more complicated, some laptops have their own performance modes. Many Asus laptops have MyAsus or Armory Crate, for example. Lenovo has the Vantage app, Dell has MyDell, and MSI laptops have MSI Center.

3. Stop applications from opening on start-up

If your laptop is slow when it first starts up, it may be because a whole bunch of apps have been given the green light to wake up with it.

Some applications such as antivirus software are critical, but most can be toggled off. As an example, I make sure apps such as Spotify, Steam and WhatsApp don’t open on startup; I only launch them when I need them.

On a MacBook, you can see which apps have this permission in Settings > General, under Open at Login. Select an app entry and click the “minus” button to remove it.

On a Windows laptop, you’ll find the list of start-up apps in Settings > Apps > Startup. Each entry has a little on/off slider.

News.title: Why the UK medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks
News.content:
The UK’s medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks, experts have warned, with the NHS dependent on a system where much of the world relies on a handful of countries for its drug supplies.

India and China are the backbone of the global medicines market, manufacturing around two-thirds of the world’s active pharmaceutical ingredients. This leaves countries exposed to factory shutdowns, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruption and sudden changes in the price or availability of raw materials, experts told The Telegraph.

“We rely now more than ever on other countries to make sure we can get access to the medicines that the vast majority of people take,” said Dr James Davies, director of research and insights at Community Pharmacy England.

Nearly all the active ingredients in the UK’s most widely used medicines are made overseas, around 80 per cent of them in China and India, leaving the NHS exposed to shocks thousands of miles beyond its control.

The resilience of Britain’s medicine supply has eroded gradually in recent years, as global instability has placed growing strain on the supply chains it depends on.

“We’ve seen more global turbulence in general,” said Dr Davies. “It’s not unique to the UK, but it’s affecting countries across Europe, across the Western world, with the Iran war, with difficulties flying things over Ukraine and Russia, and challenges with shipping in the Red Sea.”

In the UK, shortages have been reported across a wide range of products, including antibiotics, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medicines, epilepsy treatments, hormone replacement therapy, and some diabetes medicines.

The drugs most at risk are the cheapest and most widely used – statins, blood pressure pills and antibiotics – taken by millions of people and manufactured in China and India at huge scale and minimal cost.

“Some antibiotics are almost exclusively made in China,” said Dr Davies. “For some of the blood pressure medicines, they’re more likely to be made in India. But across the board, those two are where most of the raw ingredients for those active pharmaceutical ingredients come from.”

Sports.title: Banned Croatia fans watch England clash from nearby ROOF with only kids allowed in to cheer for hosts
Sports.content:

BANNED Croatia fans managed to catch a sneaky glimpse of their match against England as they watched from a nearby rooftop.

The Three Lions travelled to take on Croatia in their Nations League group on Saturday.



But the match took place without the usual home crowd due to a supporter ban given to the nation.

Reports of crowd disturbances in their March 2025 clash with France last year meant that they were not permitted to fill their home allocation for the England match.



Instead an army of 5,500 to 6,000 local children were allowed into the stadium in the port city of Rijeka, alongside 100 England supporters.

But that didn’t stop all of the local adults from finding a way to follow the action, with a number of fans finding their way to a vantage point on a nearby rooftop.

About a dozen supporters were spotted taking in the view from their cheeky spot, with one supporter apparently bringing a camping chair to make sure they caught the game in style.

But the clever plan backfired on the lot as their heroes got off to a nightmare start at home.

It took the unstoppable Harry Kane just eight minutes to find the breakthrough for the visitors.

Jude Bellingham then doubled their advantage after an impressive bit of improvisation from Anthony Gordon.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Ironically the young crowd watched their team get something of a schooling on the pitch in the first half, with Gordon adding a third thanks to a teasing cross from Jarell Quansah.

And Bukayo Saka would finally get in on the action as he turned home a cross from Bellingham directly in front of goal before the half-time break.

ITV’s Mark Pougatch joked that the fans might not be able to stomach much more before deciding to go indoors and watch something else.



The Croatian side looked out of sorts, just three games into the tenure of former West Ham boss Slaven Bilic.

They managed a 2-1 win over Czechia in their group stage opener last month, but fell to a 4-1 thumping at the hands of Spain days later.

Sports.title: ‘F*** that’ – ‘Greedy b******’ Paul Scholes demands Man Utd winners’ medal in X-rated blast after City guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED legend Paul Scholes is demanding a TWELFTH Premier League winner’s medal amid City’s financial charges.

City were found guilty of more than 100 financial breaches between 2009-18 and there have been calls for them to be stripped of their titles in 2012, 2014 and 2018.



United were pipped to the post by City in the final seconds of the 2011-12 season when Sergio Aguero lashed in a memorable added-time winner against Queens Park Rangers.

Scholes had come out of retirement midway through the season and was in influential form for United, who had an eight-point lead with six games remaining.



However, a 1-0 defeat at Wigan Athletic preceded a 4-4 draw with Everton – when United had been 4-2 up – before a cautious approach backfired in a 1-0 loss at City in early May.

City’s success marked their first title in 44 years and they have since won seven more under Manuel Pellegrini and Pep Guardiola.



Scholes was a member of 11 United title-winning squads but wants to make it a dozen.

The 51-year-old wrote on his Instagram story: “Keep hearing ex-team-mates saying they want trophies taking off them but they don’t want their medals… f*** that I’m a greedy b**** I want my medal.”

City have lodged an appeal, claiming their major sponsorships were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than owner Sheikh Mansour.

But that could be undermined by a statement by sponsors Etihad gave to a US investigation in 2015 that stressed it was “false” that the Abu Dhabi government paid for Etihad’s sponsorship.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Former United players David de Gea, Rio Ferdinand and Juan Mata have all floated the possibility of receiving retrospective winner’s medals.

Wayne Rooney said he did not want one for United’s 2012 disappointment, though.

Sports.title: Jack Wilshere lifts lid on dad’s hilarious reaction after watching Arsenal prodigy Max Dowman for first time
Sports.content:
Next

JACK WILSHERE was so impressed by a 13-year-old Max Dowman that he called his dad to come and watch him play.

And Wilshere’s father was equally as gobsmacked, telling his son that Dowman was already better than him.



Wilshere, 34, helped guide Dowman through the Arsenal youth ranks when he was in charge of the Gunners’ Under-18s side.

The former Arsenal midfielder, who won two FA Cups with the North London club, gave Dowman his debut for the U18s when he was just 13 years old.



Wilshere knows exactly what Dowman is going through, having burst onto the scene at Arsenal as a 16-year-old in similar fashion to the youngster.

But even he could not believe how good Dowman was at such a young age, needing a fresh set of eyes to back up what he was saying.

The Luton Town boss told the BBC: “He played for my U18s team when he was 13.

“I played for the 18s when I was 14 and I remember calling my dad saying, ‘You need to come and watch this kid play.’ I was like, ‘Was 13 too young?’

“Even in the first game we could clearly see that he was ready for it.

“My dad is very biased, as you could imagine. But even he said, ‘He’s better than you’.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Wilshere is still in contact with Dowman and the pair have exchanged calls and messages throughout the 16-year-old’s breakthrough into the first team.

It is not just Dowman that Wilshere helped mould during his two years as U18s boss at Arsenal, but also Myles Lewis-Skelly and Ethan Nwaneri.

Wilshere recalls watching on with pride last season as the trio helped Mikel Arteta’s side end Arsenal’s 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

He added: “I am really happy for Mikel and for his staff, because of how committed they are and how much work they have put in.



“But also the players. Myles was in there, Max was in there. I am really happy for them because they worked really hard to get there and they deserve all of it.”

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘set to return for Antonio Nusa after Christos Tzolis injury blow with Tottenham also eyeing January transfer’
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL are leading the race to sign Antonio Nusa from RB Leipzig in January.

The Gunners face stiff competition from North London rivals Tottenham after an injury to 24-year-old winger Christos Tzolis.



Premier League champions Arsenal are set to face stiff competition from several European rivals after a breakthrough Bundesliga season for the 21-year-old.

English sides Tottenham, Newcastle, and Aston Villa have also shown an interest in the youngster, according to German outlet fussball-news.



Additionally, Serie A side Roma have made initial enquiries for the 33-cap Norway star, while Bayern Munich, Barcelona, and Atletico Madrid are thought to be keeping close tabs.

SunSport previously reported that Arsenal had looked to sign Nusa during the summer transfer window.

The Gunners were set to field an offer worth £34million, however, Leipzig were not willing to let the winger leave.

Nusa arrived in Germany from Club Brugge in 2024 on a £18m (€21m) deal, becoming a key component of the team’s attack.

He is currently signed to a five-year deal worth £36,500 per week, which is set to run until 2029.

Leipzig have no intention of letting the winger move, setting a price tag of up to £55m for his services.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

This is despite Nusa’s market value being only estimated at around £38m.

Arsenal’s refreshed interest comes just days after Tzolis hobbled off during Greece’s Nations League clash against the Netherlands.

Tzolis has since been sent home from international duty with a hamstring injury, leaving Arsenal debating how to fill the void left on the wing.

Clubs will have the opportunity to bid for Nusa when the transfer window opens on Friday, January 1.

Sports.title: Former Championship star, 36, joins shock non-league club in bizarre free transfer three months after contract expired
Sports.content:
Next

AN EFL cult hero has returned to English football SIX YEARS after his last appearance on these shores.

The former second-tier menace has spent time in Italy, Malaysia and most recently Cyprus since leaving Sheffield Wednesday in 2020.



But he had been on the lookout for a new club since the expiration of his AEL Limassol contract at the end of June.

Now, Fernando Forestieri is back – at an unfamiliar level.



The Argentina-born former Italian international, 36, has been snapped up by National League North outfit Oxford City.

In their social media unveiling, the sixth-tier club called Forestieri “mercurial” and a “maverick”.

Forestieri, who had been staying sharp in a pre-season camp laid on by the PFA, said: “I’m looking forward to coming back to English football.

“The club wanted to sign me, and I’m more than happy to be here.

“I’ve missed my family a lot, so to now settle here in England and not move anymore is one of the reasons I wanted to stay here and sign here.”

Forestieri will link up with manager Ross Jenkins at third-place Oxford – a former Watford team-mate.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The forward is still fondly remembered by Hornets and Wednesday fans for his flair, fiery temperament and goal-scoring.

Forestieri bagged 21 goals in 91 games for Watford, helping them achieve promotion to the Premier League in 2015.

But instead of following them to the top flight, he headed to Hillsborough where he played some of the best football of his career.

Forestieri scored 40 goals in 134 games for the Owls, earning him a move to Serie A side Udinese.

Sports.title: Caballo De Mar upsets Scandinavia in Cadran clash
Sports.content:
Caballo De Mar brought an end to Scandinavia’s eight-race winning run when repeating his win in the Qatar Prix du Cadran from 12 months ago in a thrilling finish at ParisLongchamp.

George Scott's stayer was delivered by Oisin Murphy at the furlong marker to grab the lead from Scandinavia and the fading pacesetter Queenstown.

As the pair locked horns through the final furlong, Scandinavia regained the lead only for Caballo De Mar to fight back in the shadow of the post to get up by a neck.

Connections had to sweat through a stewards' inquiry after an objection by Ryan Moore, whose mount Scandinavia, the 1-6 favourite, appeared to receive a bump from the 9-2 winner close to the finish.

Scandinavia's sequence had included five Group Ones, but Scott's charge is a formidable opponent at his best, particularly in Paris where he is now three from three in Group Ones.

Scott said: "What an amazing performance from the horse and the team at home.

"I was very emotional afterwards - he's just such a special horse to us and to come and win the Cadran again is great.

"He's an amazing horse and just a real character. He takes a lot of managing at home, he's very lazy and it's hard to get a grip on him."

The Newmarket handler felt beforehand he had a chance of beating the red-hot favourite, adding: "We wanted to track Scandinavia and it all went to plan. We managed to get well up on him and then he fought back.

"I thought if there was an opportunity to beat him it was today because my horse loves it here, he was showing all the right signs and Scandinavia had a very hard race in Ireland last time. We felt we could beat him today, but you're not going to say something like that.

"We'll see how he comes out of it, but he could go to Ascot on Champions Day."

Aidan O'Brien said of Scandinavia: "He ran a great race and it's been a long season for him.

"The ground was a little bit on the slower side for him. Ryan said he was coming back at him.

"That will be him finished for the season. I was never going to go to Ascot as the ground would definitely be gone for him by then."

Sports.title: Rybakina suffers shock loss in first match as world No 1
Sports.content:
Elena Rybakina suffered a stunning defeat to world No 118 Alina Charaeva in her first match since becoming world No 1.

Rybakina reached the top of the world rankings after winning the US Open last month - her second Grand Slam title of 2026 - but was brought crashing back down to earth with a 6-3 4-6 3-6 defeat to Alina Charaeva at the China Open on Saturday afternoon.

Armenia's Charaeva had never faced a top-20 player before this match, but stunned the top seed to set up a round-of-32 clash with Britain's Sonay Kartal.

"I don't have words," said Charaeva after the victory of her life.

"This is incredible. Of course Elena is an amazing player who is doing really good this season winning two Grand Slams.

"For me it's just a dream come true. I just tried to stay hard mentally and keep believing I could turn around the game to my side.

"Never stop believing, I guess!"

Alcaraz battles to book quarter-finals spot at Japan Open

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alcaraz came through a tough examination on Saturday

Carlos Alcaraz battled through a gripping first-set tie-break to book a spot in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open with a 7-6 (8-6) 6-1 victory over Matteo Arnaldi.

The Spaniard will face world No 46 Denis Shapovalov in the last eight, after the Canadian defeated Alejandro Tabilo 7-5 3-6 6-4 in Tokyo.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alcaraz came back from almost losing a first-set tiebreak to seal victory

After going 2-5 down in the tie-break, Alcaraz saved four set points before flipping the decider on its head and go 1-0 up.

The world No 3 found another gear in the second set, breaking Arnaldi twice to seal victory.

"I just tried to stay there, point after point," Alcaraz said.

"I changed how I played until that moment and it worked out. I'm just happy I got that first set. Matteo was playing great."

Elsewhere in Tokyo, Jiri Lehecka came from behind to secure a 5-7 6-4 6-4 win against Ugo Humbert and set up a quarter-final clash against Adolfo Daniel Vallejo Alvarez, who knocked out Italian Matteo Berrettini.

At the China Open, US Open champion Alexander Zverev set up a blockbuster quarter-final tie against Novak Djokovic after the German No 1 seed brushed past wildcard Juncheng Shang 6-0 6-3.

After suffering a second-round defeat at the US Open, Alex de Minaur has returned to winning ways, with the Australian overcoming France's Quentin Halys in three sets on Saturday to set up a quarter-final clash with Andrey Rublev.

Image: Alex De Minaur will face off against Andrey Rublev in the quarter-finals

A spot in the semi-finals isn't the only thing up for grabs in this match, with both De Minaur and Rublev battling for Race to Turin points, as both look to secure one of the final spots at this year's ATP Finals.

Rublev booked his spot in the quarters after he bounced back from a second-set comeback from Roman Safiullin to win 6-2 3-6 6-4.

Daniil Medvedev sealed a straight-sets win over Jan-Lennard Struff, and will face the winner of Francisco Cerundolo's tie against Jakub Mensik.

Gauff returns with a win, Dart knocked out

Following her semi-final defeat to Rybakina at the US Open, Coco Gauff returned from a three-week break and booked her spot in the third round at the China Open, with a 7-6(7-4) 4-6 6-2 win over world No 66 Camila Osorio.

The two-time Grand Slam champion outlasted the Colombian in a first-set tie-break, before being broken at 4-5 to concede the following set.

Osorio battled hard in the final exchange, saving two match points, but Gauff would see out the victory and set up a tie against China's Xinran Sun in the next round.

Britain's Harriet Dart started strongly in her match against 10th seed Iva Jovic, taking the opening set.

However, she keep couldn't her foot on the accelerator, losing the next two sets in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

Sports.title: Hamilton hopes for 'awesome' Verstappen fight for win
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says it will be important for Ferrari to focus on their own race for what is expected to be a challenging Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but admits it would be "awesome" if they have the pace to stay with polesitter Max Verstappen from the front row.

​Hamilton produced "probably my best lap of the year" to claim second on the grid with his last attempt of qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit, his second front-row start of the year.

It will be the first time Verstappen and Hamilton, the grid's two-most successful drivers and the sport's biggest names, have started at the head of a Grand Prix together since July 2023, at that year's Hungarian Grand Prix.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is just behind them in third, creating a mouth-watering head of the grid for lights out at 8am on Sunday live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event.

Verstappen claimed pole, Red Bull's first of the season, by 0.298s and the Dutchman's form so far this weekend on F1's return to Sepang suggests he is the favourite to win too.

Indeed, Hamilton was staying cautious about Ferrari's chances of fighting for victory.

"I think I can be really happy with today," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1.

"I think in the last race we were not fast in the race so I don't know, pace wise, how we will be tomorrow.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of qualifying at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the Sepang International Circuit

"What I do know is we carry this deficit of straight-line speed. What that ultimately means is I think we're slightly quicker through corners, particularly low-speed corners I think we're a little bit quicker than say the Red Bulls and some of the others, but then on the straights we lose a lot.

"What that means then for the race on a track like this where degradation is very, very high, tyres are getting so hot all the time, is we have to push more through corners to try and keep up and make up for the loses in the straights.

"So that's ultimately what we have to be careful of doing too much of tomorrow [Sunday] and degrading more in trying to hold on to them. So I think we just have to run our own race, whatever that be pace wise, and not be focusing on trying to over-push to hold on.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the thrilling end to qualifying at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia!

"I think he's got the pace generally to pull away but if that's different when we start the race and we're able to hold on and we're in the fight, that'd be awesome as well. But all we can do is do our best, so I'll give it everything tomorrow."

Grand Prix distance tipped to be 'completely different ballgame'

F1 has experienced typically hot and humid conditions on the sport's first return to Malaysia in nine years but the abrasiveness of an aged Sepang track surface has created additional unexpected challenges.

Multiple pit stops are predicted in Sunday's 56-lap race, with teams expected to adopt different tyre strategies and all three tyre compounds likely to be seen.

Hamilton said after qualifying: "I'm much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track - I mean, they're overheating from the get-go.

"Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you're going to go.

"I like to think we've got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I'll just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow."

Bahrain GP Grid: Top 10 1) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



2) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



3) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



7) George Russell, Mercedes



8) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



9) Pierre Gasly, Alpine



10) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur told Sky Sports F1: "It's a good qualifying but the success is on Sunday, it's never on Saturday.

"On top, we know that this one will be a lot about degradation, about race pace, about tyre management much more than great position.

"But I prefer to have a good qualifying than not. Starting from the first and second row with Lewis and Charles [Leclerc] is a good start, but we have to now put all our focus on the race."

Verstappen eyes first 2026 win but ready for 'not straightforward' race

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player SkyPad analysis of Max Verstappen's first pole position in 2026

Verstappen's 49th career pole position was his first since the final race of last season in Abu Dhabi, also the scene of the Dutchman's most recent win.

He made clear his determination on his arrival at Sepang on Thursday to claim a victory before the 2026 campaign ended.

Speaking after qualifying first at Sepang, Verstappen told Sky Sports F1: "As a team, we want to win. We're here to win, we're not just here to grab podiums.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen reacts to 'special' pole at the Bahrian GP in Malaysia

"So, we are looking forward to it but we also know that it's not going to be that straightforward.

"There are so many things that we still need to see that have to work well, or in our favour, but we'll see tomorrow."

Verstappen won the last Malaysia Grand Prix in 2017 so is aiming for back-to-back triumphs at Sepang, albeit with an unusually-large nine year-gap in between and under different race titles.

Sports.title: Fairy Glen foils Sunly in Prix de Royallieu
Sports.content:
Fairy Glen came from last to first in the Qatar Prix de Royallieu to floor odds-on favourite Sunly and land a Group One prize for Newmarket training duo Simon and Ed Crisford.

Anchored in last place by Mickael Barzalona as Consent, Cameo, Sugar Island and Amelia Earhart cut out a decent pace in the one-mile-six-furlong contest, the five-year-old delivered a withering challenge up the straight.

Sunly, who was backed into favouritism at 5-6, had taken up the running a furlong from home, but with a target to aim at Barzalona and Fairy Glen came late and wide to grab top spot by a neck.

St Leger third Amelia Earhart battled on well to hold third place, another three-quarters of a length back.

Fairy Glen, who is set to be retired at the end of the season, won the Group Two Balanchine and Dubai Gold Cup in Meydan in the spring and finished fifth in the Prix Vicomtesse Vigier behind Caballo De Mar here in May.

She had warmed up for this with a second in a Listed contest at Yarmouth last month and Ed Crisford said: "Exactly what Mickael said would happen did happen - he said they'd get racing a long way out.

"He knows her really well from Dubai and just wanted to take his time on her. They did get racing a long way out, he was following Sunly through and she's a game filly. She's never going to win by two or three lengths, but she gets the job done.

"She probably should have won at Yarmouth a couple of weeks ago. It was her first run after a summer break and we didn't want to give her a hard race because this was the aim.

"She's a really good filly and she's won a Group One. She will be retired at the end of this year, whether there's another race for her… she is in at Ascot (on Champions Day) and there might be something back here.

"We'll talk to her owner, but we might be able to fit another race in before she goes to stud."

Wimbledon Hawkeye swoops for Prix Dollar prize

All roads lead to Bahrain for Wimbledon Hawkeye after he continued an excellent first campaign for George Scott with victory in the Qatar Prix Dollar at ParisLongchamp.

Winner of the Royal Lodge for James Owen a couple of years ago, the son of Kameko was bought privately by the Victorious Forever team during the off-season and has proved a shrewd purchase, with a Group Three win at Deauville followed by a nose defeat to Hotazhell in last month's Irish Champion Stakes.

With Christophe Soumillon again on board, Wimbledon Hawkeye was much the best horse in this Group Two contest and was good value for the winning margin of half a length over Zaydann.

"He's a class horse - he's proven that time and time again this year," said Scott.

"He was a bit fresh beforehand and I was a bit apprehensive how fresh he was, but he travelled into it like a really good horse."

Wimbledon Hawkeye's odds for the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes were widely cut, but an appearance on Champions Day at Ascot is not on the agenda.

Scott added: "I think he'll be perfect for Bahrain. Shaikh Nasser has put his foot down, there'll be no Champion Stakes. I want to do what the boss wants to do and he's right - we want to take a fresh horse to Shaikh Nasser's home.

"He was bought for Bahrain so this is all a bonus really. I'll give him a week in the field when he gets home and the Bahrain International is going to be the perfect race for him."

Of the winning rider, he added: "It's cool to be associated with Christophe. He's not someone I know very well and I've had a bit of a man crush on him since he started riding! He's got that charisma like Oisin (Murphy) and Frankie (Dettori) - they're just one-offs."

Sports.title: Ten injured as car drives into crowd gathered to support NRL team
Sports.content:
An 18-year-old man has been arrested after a vehicle drove into a crowd of people who had gathered to support the Newcastle Knights NRL team in New South Wales on Saturday, as the side trained ahead of their Grand Final against Sydney Roosters

Newcastle Knights CEO Peter Parr has expressed his deep concern after a vehicle drove into a crowd of people supporting the NRL team on Saturday, as they prepared for their Grand Final against Sydney Roosters.

Police say 10 people were injured in the incident in Wallsend, New South Wales, including several children, while the 18-year-old man driving the vehicle has been arrested.

Thousands had been cheering the team on this week as they trained ahead of Sunday's Grand Final at Accor Stadium, Australian Associated Press reported.

Two of the injured, a five-year-old girl and a 67-year-old man, are in critical condition, and the other eight are in stable condition at a hospital, according to New South Wales Police.

Those in a stable condition included another five-year-old girl and a two-year-old girl.

In a statement on Newcastle Knights' website, Parr extended the club's support to those who have been affected by the incident.

"Our thoughts and prayers are first and foremost with everyone who has been injured, their families and loved ones, and everyone who witnessed what occurred this morning," Parr said.

"What was meant to be a special morning for our community, thousands of Novocastrians coming together to farewell our team and show their support ahead of the Grand Final, has understandably turned into a distressing morning.

"We want to thank our incredible fans for the passion and support they showed our team this morning. The scenes across Newcastle demonstrated once again what this football club means to our community.

"I want to particularly acknowledge the extraordinary response of our first responders. The speed and professionalism of NSW Police, NSW Ambulance and all emergency services at the scene was remarkable.

"We also extend our deepest thanks to the doctors, nurses and entire team at John Hunter Hospital who are caring for those injured.

"I would also like to personally acknowledge NSW Police Commissioner Malcolm Lanyon for his leadership and support.

"Newcastle is a strong community. We have seen that strength throughout this week, and today we need to draw on it again with compassion, care and support for those who need it most."

Assistant Commissioner David Waddell of New South Wales Police told reporters on Saturday: "The male has been arrested.

"There were two other persons in the car. We had to get the three of them out of there because the crowd did turn on them.

"We have taken that male for mandatory drug and alcohol testing. He has now been taken to the police station where he will be dealt with, and likely charged later today."

Waddell added the crash was not believed to be related to terrorism.

"There is no concerns other than this being a tragic incident where a young person has done the wrong thing and driven irresponsibly, driven erratically, and obviously lost control of the vehicle into the crowd. But there's no, no suggestion at all that it's targeted or any ill motive," Waddell said.

12m ago 13.25 EDT 64 min: The only black mark against England tonight? Pickford has been a wee bit jittery on a couple of occasions. But nothing majorly dramatic, and in any case, it’s too late to change his eccentricities now. Share

15m ago 13.23 EDT 62 min: … which Pickford claims. His attempt to release Gordon on the counter is blocked, and Pašalić scuffs a shot before falling over backwards in the slapstick style. Croatia finding new ways to humilate themselves. Share

16m ago 13.21 EDT 61 min: Matanović has another pop from distance. This time his effort is deflected wide left, and here comes Croatia’s first corner of the game … Share

17m ago 13.21 EDT 60 min: Saka has the chance to release Gordon down the middle but can’t get the pass right. Share

18m ago 13.20 EDT 59 min: Despite Croatia’s mid-game midfield rebuild, England are still first to everything. The final whistle can’t come soon enough for the hosts, whose proud record in Rijeka is already in tatters, and it could get much worse. Share

20m ago 13.17 EDT 57 min: Modrić, 41 years old and run ragged, is replaced by Jakić. Share Updated at 13.17 EDT

21m ago 13.16 EDT 56 min: Pašalić gives up possession way too easily. Gordon intercepts and strides forward, slipping Bellingham clear down the inside-left channel. Bellingham enters the box, draws Livaković, and pulls his shot wide right. It should be six. This could end up being ten. Share

23m ago 13.15 EDT 54 min: Saka smoothly glides down the right, past three half-arsed challenges, and looks for Kane in the middle. Croatia hack clear. This is way too easy for England. Share

25m ago 13.12 EDT 52 min: Gordon rampages down the left and tears past Stanišić with absurd ease. His low cross is hacked away after a fashion, with Kane lurking. England most certainly haven’t declared. Share

26m ago 13.11 EDT 51 min: Kane drops deep and nearly releases Bellingham down the middle with a racking diagonal. Nearly, not quite. England haven’t declared. Share

28m ago 13.09 EDT 49 min: Gordon’s persistence down the left earns a corner, which Livaković punches clear. The kids, to their great credit, are still making plenty of noise. Share

29m ago 13.09 EDT 48 min: Matanović tries to float a shot over Pickford from distance. It’s off target, which is just as well, because Pickford was miles out of position, and wouldn’t have been able to claw clear. Share

30m ago 13.07 EDT 47 min: Modric is brushed off the ball with arrogant ease by Scott. This Nations League campaign increasingly looking like one step too far for the great man. Share

33m ago 13.05 EDT Croatia get the second half started. Changes were necessary, and they’ve made some alright. Matanović, Vlašić and Pašalić come on for Musa, Baturina and Petar Sučić. “India were better losing 4-0 against Brazil earlier this evening than Croatia have been against England now,” argues krishnamoorthy v. Share

39m ago 12.59 EDT Half-time postbag. “The sheer (unadulterated?) excitement from a stadium of 6,000 schoolkids is amazing. They should do this all the time” – Mark Hooper “I’m aware this isn’t the hottest of takes, but Jude Bellingham really is exceptional. I’ve seen some thrilling players for England, but I don’t remember anyone with such a sense of inevitability. If we can’t win a big trophy with him, I’m not sure we ever will” – Tom Hopkins “Modrič needs to retire gracefully. You wouldn’t find Cristiano embarrassing himself and his country like this” – Simon McMahon Share

47m ago 12.50 EDT HALF TIME: Croatia 0-4 England This is an absolute rout in the making. England could easily have scored twice as many. They’ve been relentless, rampant, brilliant … although Croatia have been beyond inept, their defence and midfield almost totally AWOL. England will fancy filling their boots some more in the second period. “There’s going to be a generation of Croatian schookids with PTSD if this carries on,” observes Stillgrizzly. “Quite cruel by England.” Share Updated at 12.51 EDT

49m ago 12.49 EDT 45 min +1: Livaković, under no pressure, shanks a pass out of play. Bellingham crosses from the right, but Gordon can’t connect properly from six yards. Croatia are so lucky that there’s only going to be one minute of added time. They’re not so lucky that there’s another whole half of football still to come. Share

52m ago 12.46 EDT 43 min: The humiliation of shipping a seventh goal in less than three halves of football has stung Croatia into action. Finally. Sucic worms his way down the right but can’t get either a shot or cross away. But they’ve upped the tempo as they look for some sort of lifeline before the break. Share

53m ago 12.44 EDT 41 min: Croatia are gifted a huge chance, Anderson shipping possession on the edge of his own box. Kovačić dances in from the left, rounds Pickford … and slices his shot wide right. It’s not Croatia’s day, is it? View image in fullscreen Croatia's Mateo Kovačić rightfully hides his face after his shocking miss. Photograph: Antonio Bronić/Reuters Share Updated at 12.52 EDT

54m ago 12.43 EDT 39 min: Livaković hoofs the frame of the goal in frustration. Croatia are facing a proper shellacking here. Mindful that they’ve never tasted competitive defeat in Rijeka, the hosts launch a desperate attack. Gvardiol crosses from the right for Sucic, who heads harmlessly off target. Share

1h ago 12.41 EDT GOAL! Croatia 0-3 England (Gordon 38) Quansah channels his inner Trent, advancing down the right and crossing for Gordon, who can’t miss with his stooping header from six yards. Wonderful cross, teeing up the in-form Gordon, who is instantly serenaded by England’s 100-strong support. View image in fullscreen England’s Anthony Gordon heads home to extend the visitors’ lead. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA View image in fullscreen Cue Gordon’s trademark celebration. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at 12.50 EDT

1h ago 12.40 EDT 37 min: … but England quickly re-establish their midfield dominance. On which subject, here’s Will Cook: “Was a bit bored and worked out that Luka Modrić is closer in age to Gary Neville than everyone in this England side apart from Pickford and Kane. Which is quite a shock.” Share

1h ago 12.39 EDT 36 min: Croatia string a few more passes together. Perhaps I shouldn’t have brought attention to it. But the hosts are finally doing something. Share

1h ago 12.37 EDT 34 min: Pickford’s poor pass out from the back is intercepted, and Kovačić, out left, nearly finds Sučić in the middle. But Scott intercepts and clears. Croatia come again, and Perišić crosses from the left. Pickford comes off his line and flaps, but he’s not punished for the error. A couple of timely reminders that England need to keep their concentration, else carelessly let Croatia back into the game. Share Updated at 12.38 EDT

1h ago 12.34 EDT 32 min: As good as England have been – their press is working like a dream – Croatia have been awful. They’ve barely strung two passes together. Share

1h ago 12.33 EDT 31 min: “So far this has been child’s play for England,” quips David Wall, because somebody had to. Share

1h ago 12.33 EDT 30 min: To be fair to the kids, they’re still making one heck of a row. Still very much enjoying themselves despite England swarming all over their heroes. Share

1h ago 12.32 EDT 29 min: Kane sashays down the inside-right channel and aims for the bottom right. The ball’s deflected wide, and nothing comes of the resulting corner. Slaven Bilic isn’t looking at his shoes any more, he’s staring straight ahead at a point roughly 1,000 yards away. Share

Sports.title: Manchester City whistleblower ready to help UK authorities in return for protection
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto, whose leaks helped to trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, is prepared to help authorities in the UK with their legal case in exchange for protection from threats, the Guardian understands.

Despite the crowdfunding campaign launched on Friday to fund a new life after leaving the protection of the Portuguese police, the whistleblower’s priority remains to cooperate, provided adequate security arrangements are in place.

In addition to the sporting ramifications of the case being conducted against City by the Premier League, British authorities could also decide to extend the inquiry. That has already occurred in Portugal in relation to some of the documents disclosed by Pinto. City were found guilty of more than 100 charges by an independent commission that unearthed “sham” contracts to boost income artificially by £900m, an investigation that was prompted by Pinto’s leaks of thousands of private documents.

City confirmed on Friday the club will appeal against the tribunal’s verdict.

With detailed knowledge of the documents, individuals and companies involved in the case – as well as documents that may have been overlooked during the investigation – Rui Pinto is willing to continue as a protected witness in another country, it is understood.

Just days before his arrest in Budapest in January 2019, the 37-year-old Portuguese national was negotiating entry into a witness protection programme in France, an initiative that was halted by the Portuguese authorities.

If it is confirmed that Rui Pinto will no longer be a protected witness in Portugal, he will be free to cooperate with authorities in other countries from 10 October. He has cooperated sporadically with French, German and Belgian authorities. The UK could now be added to that list, should it wish to do so.

Pinto’s potential contribution in the UK could extend well beyond the City furore. The hundreds of millions of files he gathered as part of Football Leaks and Luanda Leaks are not solely in the possession of the Portuguese authorities.

Between his arrest in Hungary and his extradition to Portugal, French authorities travelled to the Hungarian capital and copied the contents of all the electronic devices in the whistleblower’s possession. Rui Pinto was later acquitted of 241 counts after a second trial in Portugal in April this year.

The documents can now be shared between countries as part of international cooperation between nations with bilateral ties, including the UK.

Rui Pinto is now waiting to find out what his future holds. His defence protested against the decision of ending the protection, accusing Portugal of “state terrorism”. The whistleblower’s lawyers said they had appealed against the decision and had sought to establish how the risk assessment had been carried out but had received no response.

The hacker says he wants to leave Portugal for a secret location. At the time of writing, more than €19,000 (£16,530) had already been raised by a crowdfunding campaign.

Sports.title: Zigiotti Olme capitalises on Liverpool mistake to keep Manchester United moving up WSL
Sports.content:
Julia Zigiotti Olme’s sixth-minute lob proved enough to earn the Manchester United coach, Eva Olid, a second Women’s Super League victory of the season with a 1-0 home win over Liverpool.

Zigiotti Olme capitalised on a mistake by Liverpool goalkeeper, Khiara Keating, and, despite some late pressure by Gareth Taylor’s side, United held on to make it back-to-back league wins.

After a shaky start under the new head coach, Olid, the Spaniard has now masterminded four consecutive victories in all competitions and United are unbeaten in five matches.

This was United’s 250th match since the team reformed in 2018 and Olid watched her side mark the occasion with the breakthrough after six minutes.

It was a moment to forget for England goalkeeper Keating after her pass out from the back was intercepted by Zigiotti Olme, who composed herself and chipped home in superb fashion.

Liverpool pushed for a leveller and drew a double save from the United goalkeeper, Phallon Tullis-Joyce, midway through the first half. Cornelia Kapocs had a low effort saved by Tullis-Joyce, who got up quickly to deny Beata Olsson on the rebound as well.

United’s Jess Park hit the crossbar before half-time with a left-foot strike from the edge of the box before Keating saved at her near post from Andrea Medina on the rebound. Liverpool’s best chance of an equaliser came 20 minutes from time when Jenna Clark found herself free at a corner but she could not direct her header on target.
