Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Ticket Sales Revive The Klitschko Blueprint
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel’s reported 25,000 presale ticket sales give Frank Warren a financial reason to continue arranging manageable defenses in Germany. If Nelson Hysa attracts that level of demand, tougher opposition becomes less urgent from a business perspective.

The November 28 fight in Düsseldorf offers an early indication that Kabayel’s popularity can sell a stadium event without an established heavyweight rival.

“25,000 tickets sold in 24 hours presale for Agit Kabayel vs Nelson Hysa in Germany next month!” Warren posted on X. “Presale still open for the World Heavyweight title fight not to be missed.”

There are echoes of the Klitschko approach: build the evening around the champion, with the challenger supplying an unbeaten record and an optimistic knockout promise. Wladimir’s defense against Francesco Pianeta in Mannheim demonstrated how a less accomplished opponent could become part of a major German boxing occasion.

Warren’s figures suggest Kabayel may be developing similar commercial freedom. Overseas criticism of Hysa’s credentials has less financial consequence if local supporters keep buying seats.

That would represent a change from the fights that established Kabayel internationally. He stopped Arslanbek Makhmudov and Frank Sanchez in Riyadh, beating unbeaten contenders whose reputations made those victories meaningful. Those performances supplied evidence of his ability under pressure.

Hysa, 25-0 with 23 knockouts, offers attractive promotional numbers. At 42, however, he faces a substantial increase in opposition. Beating him would provide Kabayel with another successful defense while revealing comparatively little about his chances against the other champions.

The business calculation also extends beyond the stadium. DAZN lists the event as pay-per-view. German ticket buyers may embrace a homecoming spectacle, while international viewers could require a more competitive matchup before paying. No broadcast sales figures are available to establish that demand.

A profitable German base could help Kabayel negotiate better terms for future unifications, including offers from Saudi Arabia. He would have a credible alternative to accepting whatever purse is offered abroad.

The sporting cost comes if comfortable defenses become the routine. Kabayel has already shown he can beat dangerous contenders. Spending more of his prime proving he can sell tickets would delay the fights needed to establish how far that ability can take him.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Sacrifices Millions For Tyson Fury Fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua accepted a pay cut of at least £10 million to bring his December 11 fight with Tyson Fury to Britain, according to Eddie Hearn. The promoter believes fighting in Cardiff gives Joshua an edge, but the expected post-midnight start and Fury’s own British following complicate that calculation.

Joshua has secured familiar surroundings at the Principality Stadium. What he has not secured is a convenient fight time or a crowd certain to favor him.

“To keep it in the UK he’s got to turn down eight figures plus,” Hearn said, as reported by BoxingScene. “AJ goes to me ‘whatever you think’ and I’m like ‘no, no, no, it’s your money. I can’t make that decision for you.’”

Hearn recommended Britain because he believed it improved Joshua’s chances. Joshua accepted the sacrifice, moving the event away from a reported November 20 date at Madison Square Garden.

Staying in Britain removes transatlantic travel, but a bout beginning after midnight still requires unusual preparation. Joshua and Fury will need to be ready to perform late into the night, with the exact ring-walk time still to be set. The location offers familiarity but doesn’t eliminate the scheduling challenge.

The crowd could also be divided. Fury has his own British following, making it difficult to treat Cardiff as a straightforward home advantage for Joshua. Both men could receive substantial support.

There is a financial argument for Joshua’s decision. Beating Fury could generate a lucrative rematch and strengthen demand for his next fight, helping him recover the money surrendered here. That potential return depends on winning. Paying more to secure a preferred location does not guarantee a better performance.

British ticket buyers face their own tradeoff. They get the fight on home soil, but the expected late start accommodates American viewers on Netflix.

Turki Alalshikh claimed switching from New York to Cardiff meant losses of £53 million for the event, separate from Joshua’s reduced purse. Wembley’s 11 p.m. curfew complicated plans, while Cardiff offered a retractable roof and roughly 80,000 capacity.

Joshua has paid a high price for the venue. Whether it gives him the edge, Hearn anticipates, will only become clear once the fight begins.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Prepares For Christian Mbilli’s Relentless Pace
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is working on his stamina for Christian Mbilli, whose punch output threatens to make his October 31 return a demanding one. At 36, coming off a defeat, elbow surgery, and more than a year outside the ring, Canelo faces an opponent capable of making him work when he would prefer a breather.

The timing makes this dangerous. Canelo has years of experience finding openings against aggressive fighters, but exploiting those openings requires him to keep answering. Mbilli’s willingness to throw repeatedly could turn Canelo’s pauses between attacks into stretches where the challenger is being outworked.

“We know he’s a fighter with a lot of stamina, who throws a lot of punches,” Canelo said to ESPN MX. “We have the experience. Obviously, we’ve been working very hard on having the stamina ourselves to be able to respond in the same way.”

That acknowledgment gets to the toughest part of this matchup. Canelo can land the cleaner, harder shot in an exchange and still spend the rest of the minute defending. If Mbilli keeps attacking after being countered, Canelo will need more than occasional eye-catching punches to control rounds.

Body punching offers Canelo a way to slow that pace. Mbilli’s aggression should give him opportunities to counter downstairs, but he has to take them early and consistently. Waiting for the perfect opening while absorbing combinations would allow Mbilli to dictate how much work each round demands.

Age and accumulated wear make that harder to sustain. Surgery does not establish that Canelo will return diminished, but this will be his first fight since the procedure. A high-output opponent is a demanding test of whether he can repeatedly punch, defend and reset under pressure.

Canelo argues that Mbilli has never faced anyone with his experience. That may help him anticipate attacks. The question is whether he can keep producing the answers for twelve rounds when Mbilli refuses to give him time off.

Sports.title: Sandor Martin Favors Ryan Garcia Against Isaac Cruz
Sports.content:
Sandor Martin favors Ryan Garcia against Isaac Cruz in a potential welterweight fight, questioning whether Cruz could overcome Ryan’s physical advantages after moving up from 140 pounds.

Martin believes Cruz could drop Ryan, but reaching him would be the harder part. Cruz would have to cross a taller opponent’s punching range repeatedly, making the quality of his entries more important than simply maintaining pressure.

Cruz is one of the options Ryan is considering for his next fight in December, although Ryan has yet to choose an opponent. Ryan’s drawing power gives him greater control over that decision, leaving Cruz waiting to see whether the opportunity materializes.

“Pitbull’s knockout power, despite him being a powerful puncher, decreased at 140,” Martin said in to Luis Parra. “Can a punch from Pitbull put Ryan Garcia on the canvas? I think so. Now, will he have the tools to land that punch? We have to see it in the ring. I think Ryan Garcia starts as the favorite because of his physical advantage, but Pitbull has his chances.”

Marching straight ahead would invite Ryan’s left hook. Cruz would need to feint, draw the lead punch, and move underneath it, then cut off Ryan’s retreat rather than follow him around the ring. Predictable timing would give Ryan repeated opportunities to land his best shot.

Ryan’s upright exits could give Cruz an opening. If Ryan pulls straight back without moving far enough to escape, another step could bring Cruz into position to attack the body. Staying close would force Ryan to defend combinations instead of setting his feet for another hook.

That makes the first exchange crucial. Ryan could punish a careless entry, but throwing his opening punch would not finish the defensive work. If Cruz gets underneath it, Ryan would need to turn away or tie him up before the pressure becomes sustained.

Cruz’s footwork would also affect his stamina. Chasing would consume energy without guaranteeing chances to punch; forcing Ryan toward the ropes would create more useful exchanges. Martin’s preference is understandable, but Cruz’s chances would depend on making Ryan fight at close quarters often enough to overcome those physical advantages.

Sports.title: Omari Jones Stops Alan Sanchez In Two Rounds
Sports.content:
Omari Jones ended his run of three consecutive decision wins by stopping Alan Sanchez in the second round Friday night, October 2, at Caribe Royale Orlando. The hometown prospect finished his first professional main event with the early stoppage he had been seeking.

Referee Christopher Young intervened at 49 seconds of round two. Jones improved to 8-0 with five knockouts, while Sanchez dropped to 24-8-1 with 10 KOs. The scheduled eight-round junior middleweight fight headlined Project Series 2 on DAZN.

Jones pressed forward and put combinations together, forcing Sanchez into a defensive fight. Once the veteran was hurt near the ropes in the second, Jones kept punching until the referee stepped between them. It was a finish built through sustained offense rather than one punch suddenly ending the contest.

That was the useful part of the performance. Jones recognized an opportunity and increased his output before Sanchez could recover. For a prospect coming off three distance fights, converting that opening into a stoppage gave this appearance a different outcome from his recent outings.

OMARI JONES GETS IT DONE IN TWO ROUNDS! 🔥#JonesSanchez ▪️ pic.twitter.com/msHkJwLv0u — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 3, 2026

The opponent also puts the result in perspective. Sanchez entered at 35 and had been inactive since May 2025, when Nicklaus Flaz stopped him. His experience offered Jones a veteran to work against, but this was a favorable matchup for the younger fighter rather than a test against a rising contender.

Jones, 23, won bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics before turning professional in March 2025. His first four professional victories came inside the distance, followed by three decisions.

Friday’s win adds another stoppage without answering every question about his development. Sanchez could not make him sustain that aggression through a long fight or punish him for committing to combinations.

A more durable opponent who punches back under pressure would provide a better measure of how Jones’s attacking approach holds up. For this hometown headliner, he handled the available task quickly and kept his unbeaten record intact.

Ghana News.title: NPP National Delegates Conference: Nhyiaeso MP calls for unity and peace
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament for Nhyiaeso, Stephen Amoah, has called on members of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) to prioritise unity and peace as the party holds its National Delegates Conference in Kumasi.

Speaking at the conference on Saturday, 3 October, Mr Amoah said the most important consideration for delegates should be the election of national executives who have the competence and leadership qualities required to help the party win its next election.

“I expect that we get a set of national executives that can actually help us to win the elections. I think that's the most important thing,” he said.

He emphasised that the party needs competent national executives with what it takes to develop an effective strategy to win power from the NDC.

According to him, the NPP’s ultimate objective should remain its return to government, choosing national executives a critical decision for delegates at the conference.

Mr Amoah, however, stressed that the leadership contest should not undermine the unity of the party or create divisions among its members.

He urged delegates and other party members to ensure that the conference is conducted peacefully, saying unity should remain a fundamental principle throughout the process.

“I also expect that the most important fundamental elements of unity will prevail here in peace,” he said.

His comments come at a significant moment for the NPP as delegates gather to elect national executives who will take responsibility for leading the party and shaping its direction ahead of the next general election.

For Mr Amoah, the leadership elections should therefore be viewed beyond individual ambitions, with the broader interests and electoral prospects of the party remaining central to the process.

He said the NPP needs a leadership team capable of working towards the common objective of winning power, while ensuring that the process of selecting those leaders does not damage the cohesion of the party.

Ghana News.title: Cargill Ghana renovates, equips ICT laboratory for Ahmadiyya Basic School
Ghana News.content:
Cargill Ghana Limited, through its Cargill Cares initiative, has renovated and equipped an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) laboratory at the Ahmadiyya Basic School in Tema to support digital education and skills development.

The project involved the conversion of an existing classroom into a modern ICT laboratory equipped with 32 computers and monitors, a printer, 20 computer tables, 40 chairs, air-conditioning units, security doors, a television and internet connectivity.

Speaking at the handover ceremony, Managing Director of Cargill Ghana Limited, Max Essoh Latte, said the investment forms part of the company’s commitment to creating opportunities for young people through education.

“At Cargill, we believe that education is one of the most powerful ways to create opportunities and build stronger communities. By providing students with access to technology and a modern learning environment, we hope this facility will inspire them to develop the digital skills they need to succeed in an increasingly technology-driven world.”

Mr Latte said the project was made possible through collaboration with the school and relevant education stakeholders, adding that the company was pleased to contribute to the development of young people in the Tema community.

The Municipal Director of Education, Sophia Ako, commended Cargill Ghana for the initiative, stressing the importance of private-sector partnerships in improving educational outcomes.

A representative of the Head of the Ahmadiyya Mission, Adam Kofi Yamoah, also expressed appreciation to Cargill Ghana, saying the facility would improve students’ and teachers’ access to technology and support teaching and learning.

The handover ceremony brought together representatives of Cargill Ghana, the Ghana Education Service, the Ahmadiyya Mission, school leadership, teachers, students and other stakeholders.

The newly renovated laboratory is expected to provide students and teachers with access to digital tools and internet-based learning resources while strengthening the school’s capacity to deliver ICT education.

Ghana News.title: GH¢6,500 cocoa promise has turned out to be a scam – Bawumia
Ghana News.content:
New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has criticised the Mahama administration for not fulfilling its promises to cocoa farmers.

Speaking at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 3, Dr Bawumia said the government’s promise to increase the producer price of cocoa to GH¢6,500 had not been delivered.

“The promises to cocoa farmers to increase the cocoa price to GH¢6,500 has turned out to be a scam,” Dr Bawumia said.

He also criticised the government over its promises to introduce automatic posting for teachers and nurses and improve their conditions of service.

“The promise of automatic posting of teachers and nurses and the improvement in their conditions of service has turned out to be another scam,” he said.

Dr Bawumia further accused the government of failing to fulfil its promise to cancel the teacher licensure examinations and to pay customers affected by the collapse of Menzgold and other financial institutions.

“The promise to cancel teacher licensure examinations has proven to be another scam, just as the promise to pay all Menzgold customers and customers of all financial institutions which collapsed,” he said.

He added that the government’s much-touted Nkoko Nkitikiti programme had also failed to meet expectations.

Dr Bawumia described the issues as part of what he called the record of the NDC government after two years in office.

“This is the record of the NDC two years on. As our elders say, ‘Agoro no be so a na afri anopa’. Ghana deserves better,” he said.

He assured supporters that an NPP government, if elected in 2029, would draw lessons from its previous administration, including both its successes and challenges, to improve governance.

“I assure you that when the NPP assumes the reins of office in 2029, by the grace of God, we shall bring to bear the lessons of our successes and challenges to do a way better job in these and other areas than this NDC government is doing,” Dr Bawumia said.

Ghana News.title: Firefighters battle blaze behind Amasaman China Mall
Ghana News.content:
A fire outbreak has been reported at Amasaman, behind the China Mall, with personnel from four Ghana National Fire Service stations deployed to the scene.

Firefighters from Amasaman, National Headquarters, Madina and Abelemkpe are currently working to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to nearby structures.

The incident comes just days after a separate fire outbreak at a Duraplast factory in the North Industrial Area, which destroyed property and reportedly affected the livelihoods of several workers.

The cause of the latest fire, the extent of the damage and whether there are any casualties remain unclear at this time.

Emergency personnel remain at the scene as efforts continue to bring the situation under control.

Further details are expected as firefighters assess the extent of the incident and work to secure the surrounding area.

Ghana News.title: We’ll pursue accountability despite intimidation – Afenyo-Markin
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has accused the Mahama government of trying to frighten and silence its critics, saying the minority will continue to demand accountability.

Speaking at the NPP's National Delegates Congress in Kumasi on Saturday, 3 October, Mr Afenyo-Markin said critics of the government should be allowed to express their views without fear of arrest or imprisonment.

Afenyo-Markin said the government’s actions were aimed at intimidating critics, arguing that the previous Akufo-Addo administration endured harsher criticism. “Critics are arrested and jailed for saying things the NDC government doesn't like. Under Akufo-Addo, we heard worse things against Akufo-Addo, but we endured,” he said.

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the NPP would continue to use democratic and parliamentary processes to scrutinise the government's decisions, insisting that the opposition would not be intimidated.

"We will defend our freedoms and pursue accountability through democratic means. We, the Minority, shall never be intimidated in Parliament; we will fight for you till we gain power in 2028. They want critics tired, afraid," he said.

He subsequently called on members of the NPP and the Minority to be more assertive in challenging government policies and decisions.

"Let's hold the government accountable without fear of arrest and intimidation," he said, stressing that the opposition had a responsibility to scrutinise the administration on behalf of the electorate.

Call for party unity

The Minority Leader also used his address to rally NPP members around the party's reorganisation and its preparations for the 2028 general election.

He described the party's presidential candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, as "a doer and problem solver" and urged party members to unite behind the leadership as the NPP seeks to rebuild after its return to opposition.

Mr Afenyo-Markin expressed confidence in the party's prospects, telling supporters: "The Lord is with us; come 2028, we shall prevail."

Kufuor urges careful choice of party leaders

Former President John Agyekum Kufuor also addressed the congress through a video message, calling on delegates to carefully consider the qualities required of the party's next generation of national leaders.

Mr Kufuor said Ghana needed the NPP to contribute to the country's pursuit of prosperity and transformation.

"Ghana needs NPP to lead to prosperity and transformation," he said.

He urged delegates selecting the new national executive committee to focus on leadership capable of restoring public confidence in the party.

He also invoked the principle of popular sovereignty, calling on the party to demonstrate "true respect for the idea that true sovereignty is with the people".

Akufo-Addo backs Bawumia for 2028

Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo also addressed the gathering, expressing confidence that the NPP could return to government in 2028 under Dr Bawumia.

"With God's guidance, we will emerge victorious as we did in 2000 and 2016 and form the government in 2028 with Dr Bawumia," he said.

The positions include National Chairman, Vice Chairman, General Secretary, National Organiser, National Women's Organiser, National Youth Organiser, National Nasara Organiser, National Treasurer and National Communications Director.

Ghana News.title: ‘Ghana Jollof’: Restoring the flavor
Ghana News.content:
Kwesi Yankah

Ghana Jollof, originally a state cuisine, has suddenly entered partisan politics, and could tip the scales if one party decides to swear an affidavit changing its name to ‘Ghana Jollof Party.’ Their symbol could be simple: Jollof Rice with bow-legged fried plantains!

The demand for Jollof rice has boomed overnight across the country this September, one party salivating and brandishing jollof as they advance towards their party elections early October, and tourists exercising caution at restaurants in their choice of jollof, fearing possible deportation if they make the wrong call for Jollof.

Were you surprised hearing unconfirmed reports that our Jubilee House had revised its menu card, replacing ‘Jollof Rice’ with ‘Waakye’ to dissociate itself from a social media terror who carried the name ‘Ghana Jollof.’ To boldly display jollof on a state menu perhaps amounted to glorifying a ‘despicable’ persona who of late vilifies JDM and his Government: subjecting them to vulgar abuse and tearing them apart.

Call ‘Ghana Jollof’ a faceless woman of venom who targets celebrities in Government and reduces them to garbage. In reality though the verbal terror could simply be an anonymous counterfoil to social Injustice.

Specializing in vulgar abuse, she has hurled venom at the presidency and associated units, breathing hard on perceived scandals in high places. ‘Ghana Jollof’ cuts lofty Government personalities to size with words that are too weighty for civilized lips.

References to the nether parts of the human anatomy are neither hushed nor muted, but amplified with gory details, sometimes degrading motherhood and the sacred sites of reproduction. These are not festival insults nor vulgarisms often defined by time and space; but free range ‘maledicta’ profusely splashed and celebrated by a social media that glorifies the bizarre.

If this is rather unusual for a polite society like Ghana, please consider the following explanation by ‘Ghana Jollof’ herself about what has driven her sordid outbursts:

“The Holy Bible we all know condemns injustice (atɛnkyea). The Bible itself denounces bearing false witness…We were all in this town, when KT insulted all manner of men..: dignified pastors, politicians, churches, judges, virtually all manner of people. He took on women, journalists, celebrities: ‘this one is ugly…this one has no behinds, you are like this, like that…' When he starts insulting women, he goes all out: ‘I will display your underpants,’ etc.

He insulted the courts and judges in 2020 and a court warrant was issued for his arrest while NPP was in power. When the NDC took over, the Supreme court set aside the arrest warrant and freed him. After that he resumed his insults on virtually anybody. One pastor came and confessed that he himself helped the NDC to bury 32 cows to ensure electoral victory in 2024. No one arrested him. Yet when one lady from the opposition quoted the pastor’s word, she was rather arrested and is currently in jail for a year… Was this fair? That’s what infuriates me and brings me to my feet.

“If the Bible will not be obeyed, let’s all join the insults; perhaps that could change the situation. Kelvin has indulged in insults for years… It’s my intention here to simply demonstrate that we also know their secrets…, so they can feel the pain of being at the receiving end of insults. We are all Ghanaians.

We all contributed to building this nation with our taxes. Why are some people treated differently from others? We are facing racism abroad; why should we return home to face the same discrimination? That is why I have jumped to my feet; it is to enable them empathize. Nobody has hired me to do this; neither has anyone ever spoken to me. But I am not despaired…I only want to demonstrate that ‘you end up tasting your own poison if you seek to poison others.’

The Bible has said ‘Parents, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up to the training of the Lord (Ephesians 6:4) .’ What JDM has done is to provoke his children to anger. If the church will join hands with the Peace Council, and together with JDM get Kelvin to cease fire, I will also cease fire…”

Those are the words of ‘Ghana Jollof,’ in a solemn broadcast in the Social Media. She seeks a collective search by civil society for justice. But all is not lost. Let Kelvin stop the booming war drums (kukrukukru), and the jingling echoes (kekɛkekɛ) will naturally cease.

Ghana, let’s work together to restore decency in the social media, and regain the unifying flavor of our great national cuisine. We extend this plea to JDM, ‘Father for All.’ Not JDM: ‘President of the National Democratic Congress.’

'Monkye no'

Mekɔ!

Ghana News.title: SSNIT outlines plans to transform Labadi beachfront into tourism hub
Ghana News.content:
The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) says the redevelopment of the beachfront adjoining Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach is intended to transform the area into a properly planned tourism destination while creating wider economic opportunities for the surrounding community.

“Creating a better organised tourism environment is not simply about taking away people’s livelihoods. It is about creating an enclave that can generate more sustainable and wider economic opportunities for the surrounding community,” SSNIT said.

The Trust said the recent clearance of unauthorised structures marked the beginning of a broader redevelopment effort aimed at positioning the beachfront as a major tourism and hospitality destination.

SSNIT said young people from Labadi and neighbouring communities would be considered for employment opportunities arising from the development and subsequent operations of the enclave, subject to relevant recruitment requirements.

“The redevelopment is expected to create opportunities in construction, hospitality, tourism, food services, entertainment, security, cleaning, maintenance, transportation and various related activities,” it said.

The Trust also stressed that the properties being protected and redeveloped form part of its investment portfolio, which ultimately belongs to workers and pensioners whose contributions underpin the Scheme.

“These assets belong to the workers and pensioners whose contributions form the foundation of the Scheme,” SSNIT said, adding that its responsibility was to ensure that they were “properly protected, managed and developed” to generate sustainable returns for members.

SSNIT said it would continue engaging the Chiefs, traditional authorities, community leaders and residents of Labadi throughout the redevelopment process.

“The success of the redevelopment will depend, in part, on meaningful engagement with the people who live and work in the area,” the Trust said, adding that the engagements would help identify opportunities for local participation and ensure the community understood how it could benefit.

The redevelopment of the beachfront is expected to commence this month, with SSNIT emphasising that the beach will remain open to the public.

“The beachfront will remain a public beach,” the Trust said, noting that the project would focus on restoring the area into a cleaner, safer and properly managed environment, with attention to sanitation, environmental management, security, accessibility and the overall visitor experience.

“For SSNIT, the ultimate objective is to transform the area into an asset that works better for Ghana — for visitors, the surrounding community, the tourism industry and, importantly, for members whose contributions underpin the Scheme,” the Trust said.

Ghana News.title: Today marks the beginning of a glorious chapter of the NPP – Bawumia
Ghana News.content:
Flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has described Saturday, October 3, as the beginning of a glorious chapter for the party as it elects new national executives ahead of the 2028 general elections.

He urged all aspirants contesting the various positions to accept the outcome of the elections in good faith and remain committed to the party's collective interest.

"Please accept the results in good faith," he said in his address at the NPP's National Delegates Congress in Kumasi on Saturday.

The congress is expected to produce a new crop of national executives to lead the party's reorganisation and preparations towards the 2028 general elections.

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, in his address, called on the NPP and the Minority in Parliament to remain bold in holding the government of President John Dramani Mahama accountable for its decisions.

He urged party members and the Minority to discharge their oversight responsibilities without fear of arrest or intimidation.

"Let's hold the government accountable without fear of arrest and intimidation," he said.

Mr Afenyo-Markin also expressed confidence in Dr Bawumia's leadership, describing the NPP flagbearer as "a doer and problem solver".

He called on party members to unite, support the reorganisation process and rally behind Dr Bawumia as the party prepares for the 2028 elections.

"The Lord is with us; come 2028, we shall prevail," he said.

Former President John Agyekum Kufuor, in a video message played at the congress, said Ghanaians were yearning for the NPP to return to government, adding that the party was needed to steer the country towards prosperity and transformation.

"Ghana needs NPP to lead to prosperity and transformation," he said.

Mr Kufuor urged delegates to carefully consider the qualities of the candidates seeking national executive positions, stressing the need to elect leaders capable of restoring public confidence in the party.

"So, even as we meet to pick our new crop of leaders, I want to appeal to all of you: let us, for now, select the national executive committee of the party on the careful examination to find out the sort of leadership that will enable us to regain the confidence of the people of Ghana. Let us show true respect for the idea that true sovereignty is with the people."

He emphasised the importance of respecting the will of the people as the party selects leaders to guide its affairs and strengthen its position ahead of the next general elections.

Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo also expressed confidence in the party's prospects, saying he believed the NPP would return to power in 2028 under the leadership of Dr Bawumia.

"With God's guidance, we will emerge victorious as we did in 2000 and 2016 and form the government in 2028 with Dr Bawumia," he said.

The NPP is holding its National Delegates Congress and national officers' elections in Kumasi, where delegates are voting to elect the party's next national executives.

The congress also provides a platform for the consideration of proposed constitutional amendments aimed at guiding the party's internal administration and organisational structure.

The elections form part of the NPP's broader reorganisation efforts as it seeks to consolidate its structures, strengthen unity among members and prepare for the 2028 general elections.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Somalia won’t accept Israeli presence ‘under any circumstances’: President
World.content:
In exclusive Al Jazeera interview, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud says attempts to pull Somalia into Middle East crises won’t succeed.

Somalia will not accept Israeli presence in the country “under any circumstances” and will resist any attempts to be pulled into the Middle East’s crises, its President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud tells Al Jazeera.

Speaking in an exclusive interview, Mohamud said that Israel was planning to establish a naval base in Berbera and use the city’s airport, adding that its real aim was to get closer to the Gulf states and Iran.

Berbera is a port city on the Gulf of Aden coast in Somaliland – the self-declared republic in northwestern Somalia that Israel recognised last year, but which is claimed by Mogadishu.

Berbera faces Yemen across the water near the strategic Bab al-Mandeb strait. The Iran-aligned Houthis have previously enforced a blockade on Israel-linked ships in the area.

“We will overcome the challenges posed to our country by Israeli moves,” Mohamud said in his wide-ranging interview.

He added that the Israeli plans fall under the “Greater Israel” project – referring to a term for various proposals, often rooted in biblical interpretations, for Israeli control over territory beyond its current borders. Some versions extend from the Nile to the Euphrates.

Israel has not adopted it as official policy, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an August 2025 interview that he felt connected to the vision, prompting condemnation from Arab governments.

The Somali president described Israel as a “destabilising force” that does not abide by international law.

He also criticised Tel Aviv’s recognition of Somaliland in December.



No country other than Israel recognises Somaliland, while the region’s own residents are completely opposed to an Israeli presence, Mohamud said.

Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 and has governed itself independently for more than three decades. But it had not secured recognition from any United Nations member state until Israel’s move.

Fight against armed groups

The Somali president told Al Jazeera the United States remains his country’s strongest partner in the fight against “terrorism”, and added that al-Shabab has no presence in the major cities, leaving no possibility of the group taking control in Somalia.

Al-Shabab is a Somali armed group that emerged from the Islamic Courts Union in the mid-2000s and pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012. It has fought Somalia’s federal government for years, holds territory in parts of southern and central Somalia, and has carried out deadly attacks, including in Mogadishu and in neighbouring Kenya.

Regarding the East Africa region, Mohamud said Somalia’s relations with neighbouring Ethiopia are good, and Mogadishu does not object to Addis Ababa gaining access to the sea through a joint agreement to use Somali ports for its economic interests.

Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea became independent in 1993 and relies largely on Djibouti’s ports for trade. In January 2024, Addis Ababa signed a memorandum of understanding with Somaliland on sea access, which Somalia condemned as a violation of its sovereignty. Somalia and Ethiopia later agreed to ease tensions.

Houthis ‘destabilising’ region

Mohamud also accused Yemen’s Houthis of “destabilising” the region and disrupting navigation in the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

His comments come as the group attempts to build on its lightning offensive that captured the country’s Red Sea coast last month.

Thus far, Yemeni government forces have been able to hold their positions on the front lines and even claimed to have inflicted heavy losses against the Houthis.

The Houthis have also intensified their attacks on Saudi Arabia, but the kingdom’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) has promised not to compromise on its security, saying the Yemeni rebels chose “chaos and destruction, threatening the Yemeni people and the region”.

The full interview with President Mohamud will be broadcast on Al Jazeera Arabic on Sunday.
