World.title: Construction begins on first phase of Iraq’s Madinat Al Ward
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ORA Iraq awarded CRC Dorra the building contract for the first phase of Madinat Al Ward, paving the way for large-scale development in Iraq.

The deal was signed in the presence of Naguib Sawiris, Chairman of ORA, and Mohamed Dorra, Vice Chairman of Dorra Group, as the project progressed from ground preparation to primary construction.

CRC Dorra will begin construction after POWERCHINA has completed the earthworks and ground preparation for Phase One, according to ORA Iraq.

The deal adds another important regional contractor to the development.

CRC Dorra is the contracting arm of Dorra Group, an engineering and construction business founded in 1943 that operates in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Iraq.

Its work includes residential, commercial, office, and hotel developments, as well as design-build projects.

ORA said that the selection was based on CRC Dorra’s construction expertise and capacity to perform large-scale projects.

The commencement of construction marks a key milestone for Madinat Al Ward as ORA expands its investment and development efforts in the Iraqi market.

The company said that it continues to be dedicated to building the project as an integrated community, with the new contract advancing Phase One from site preparation to physical construction.

World.title: US Treasury approves waiver for Iranian flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Foreign Affairs Fuad Hussein announced on Friday, October 2, 2026, that U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent has agreed to exempt religious pilgrimage flights to holy sites in Iraq from secondary sanctions imposed on Iranian aviation, following intensive bilateral talks held in Washington.

The decision resolves mounting diplomatic friction surrounding the status of Najaf International Airport, granting legal clarity for passenger arrivals while shielding Iraqi aviation infrastructure from punitive measures.

In a statement shared on X (formerly Twitter) and reported by the 964 Network, Hussein outlined that discussions with Bessent encompassed the overarching trajectory of U.S.-Iraqi economic and security ties, regional fiscal stability, and the spillover impacts of American sanctions enforcement on the domestic Iraqi economy.

Hussein specifically raised the operational paralysis facing Najaf International Airport—a vital national transport hub serving millions of international religious pilgrims annually—emphasizing that economic restrictions should not impede lawful civilian travel or religious observances. Secretary Bessent acknowledged Iraq’s sovereign concerns, formally approving a targeted waiver for flights directed toward the holy shrines.

During the diplomatic session, Hussein reaffirmed Baghdad’s appreciation for past U.S. and International Coalition support in the campaign to defeat Daesh (ISIS), while reiterating the federal government’s constitutional roadmap under Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi to monopolize arms under the state and maintain sole authority over war and peace.

Commending Washington’s accommodation, Hussein noted that recognizing the importance of religious freedom and facilitating pilgrim transit reflects shared values of mutual respect and tolerance, reinforcing a stable, long-term bilateral partnership between Iraq and the United States.

World.title: ITEX 2026: Iraqi AI and tech startups expand
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi, regional, and international technology enterprises showcased cutting-edge solutions in artificial intelligence, network synchronization, and enterprise digital transformation during their participation in the Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition in Baghdad.

The participating companies expressed strong ambition to expand operations and capture growing commercial opportunities in Iraq’s rapidly developing technological sector.

Hassan Abdul-Baqi Khalaf, founder of domestic startup Al-Burhan for AI Image and Video Recognition, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the venture originated from registered patents specializing in automated media verification and tamper protection against digital forgery and deepfakes.

Khalaf—a computer science student at the American University of Iraq – Baghdad (AUIB) collaborating with a doctoral partner in mathematics and physics—highlighted that their platform processes requests for more than 3,000 daily active users across private corporate clients and the public.

Delivering up to 95 percent accuracy in identifying manipulated content, the company is leveraging its inaugural exhibition presence to pursue operational partnerships with federal entities, specifically the Ministry of Interior, to detect fabricated media and enhance sovereign cyber verification tools.

International infrastructure providers also underscored their entry into the domestic market. Engineer Ahmed Mustafa of Canada’s Al-Mamas, an IT and network engineering specialist, revealed that the firm is seeking to establish an operational foothold in Iraq following successful deployments in the UAE, Qatar, and Egypt.

Al-Mamas holds exclusive distribution rights across the Middle East and North Africa for precision German-manufactured timing and synchronization hardware, which is critical for maintaining ultra-low-latency architectures across telecommunications networks, industrial automation, data center facilities, and distributed artificial intelligence systems.

Highlighting regional corporate expansion, Samer Al-Yasin, sales director for Qatar-headquartered conglomerate Mannai Corporation, affirmed that Iraq represents a fertile and attractive destination for long-term tech investment.

Marking its second exhibition appearance in Baghdad, Mannai—which employs over 15,000 personnel across the Gulf—formally established its Baghdad branch three months ago and is actively preparing to launch regional offices in Erbil and Basra.

Al-Yasin emphasized that the group is deploying enterprise digital transformation, cloud integration, and systems architecture tailored for federal ministries, banking institutions, and healthcare providers, aiming to transfer its regional technical expertise to drive national modernization and support sovereign institutional revenues.

World.title: Baghdad hosts major motorsports festival to celebrate Iraqi sovereignty day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad hosted a mass motorsports festival on Friday, October 2, 2026, to celebrate Iraqi Sovereignty Day and National Day, organized under the auspices of Iraqi National Olympic Committee President Aqeel Muften and drawing substantial public crowds alongside national sports figures.

The festival, co-organized by the Iraqi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation and secured by the Baghdad Operations Command, showcased competitive and exhibition motorsport performances to highlight domestic stability and nationwide celebrations marking the complete withdrawal of foreign forces.

Farooq Al-Rubaie, President of the Iraqi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that celebrating Sovereignty Day honors the resilience and immense sacrifices made by the armed forces and citizens over challenging decades.

Noting the passionate grassroots fanbase for motorsports across Iraq, Al-Rubaie emphasized that staging the festival serves both an athletic and patriotic duty, projecting the reality of a secure and revitalized capital. He urged local and regional media outlets along with content creators to spotlight Iraq’s stability, community engagements, and peaceful public life during major national milestones.

Baghdad Operations Command Media Director, Major General Abbas Hamid, stated to INA that Sovereignty Day—coinciding with Iraq’s National Day—reflects the sovereign resolve of the Iraqi people.

Hamid confirmed that joint security formations under the Ministries of Defense and Interior, alongside military intelligence branches, established comprehensive security perimeters around the capital to safeguard wide-ranging cultural, artistic, and athletic gatherings.

Reaffirming that Baghdad is entering an era defined by urban reconstruction and civic stability, Hamid reiterated the full readiness of security apparatuses to protect public safety and preserve social cohesion across all urban centers.

World.title: Iraq inks data center MoU with Huawei as tech giant employs 10,000 across country
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Communications formalized a strategic partnership with global telecommunications giant Huawei on Friday, October 2, 2026, signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to construct modern enterprise data centers across the country.

Finalized during the 5th Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition and Conference (ITEX 2026) in Baghdad, the agreement was concluded under the sponsorship and in the presence of Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad between the state-owned General Company for Communications and Informatics and Huawei’s executive leadership.

The initiative is aimed at bolstering Iraq’s sovereign cloud hosting, elevating service quality, and broadening international technical cooperation.

On the sidelines of the expo, Huawei confirmed the extensive scope of its commercial footprint in Iraq, revealing that it actively partners with more than 240 domestic Iraqi enterprises across diverse sectors.

Rafid Abbas Al-Khafaji, Vice President and Board Member of Huawei Iraq, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that this marked the company’s inaugural participation as an exhibitor at ITEX, expressing admiration for the high caliber of domestic and multinational engagement.

Al-Khafaji noted that Huawei presented specialized end-to-end solutions spanning oil and gas digitalization, telecommunications, smart transportation, healthcare systems, artificial intelligence, and modular data center architecture.

Reviewing the company’s continuous commercial presence in Iraq since 2003, Al-Khafaji emphasized that Huawei remained fully operational through all domestic security and economic challenges, including uninterrupted on-site work by its Chinese engineering teams during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Today, the corporation operates four major regional branches in Baghdad, Basra, Erbil, and Sulaymaniyah, supporting a wider ecosystem of over 10,000 employees.

Addressing public misconceptions, Al-Khafaji clarified that while Huawei is widely recognized among consumers for consumer smartphones, handset sales represent the smallest segment of its business portfolio by volume.

The firm’s enterprise and carrier operations form the backbone of its Iraqi footprint, servicing major mobile network operators alongside key sovereign institutions, including the Ministries of Oil, Transport, Interior, and Defense, as well as the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers.

Beyond central government networks, Huawei is driving provincial smart security solutions—such as Babylon Governorate’s integrated municipal surveillance network—while advancing intelligent electric vehicle systems and cloud infrastructures designed to anchor Iraq’s next-generation digital economy.

World.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

The grinding conflict, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, has largely focused on ground fighting in the east, with Kyiv largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontline.

But Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing.

“The capital is in a very dramatic situation,” he posted on Telegram. “It’s no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime.

“The enemy is tearing Kyiv apart.”

His message came as the authorities shut one of Kyiv’s main bridges and restricted movement on a second after another wave of deadly strikes by fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes — or even made their way on foot.

“I’ve been travelling for three hours… to get to work,” said Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam.

“There’s just no way to get there. Nothing. It’s impossible to cross the bridges today,” she told AFP.

Traffic built up due to the complete closure to all vehicles going in both directions on the Southern Bridge, one of eight bridges connecting the east and west of Kyiv over the Dnipro river.

It was hit several times on Thursday and Friday morning.

The Paton Bridge, further north, was open in one direction only, though there were no reports that it had been struck.

In a post on X, Zelensky accused Putin of last month declaring there were “no rules now”, citing unnamed intelligence and people around Putin.

“The Russians couldn’t occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings,” Zelensky said.

The Kremlin made no immediate public response to the claim, which Zelensky first made in an interview with the Financial Times.

– Daily disruption –

Kyiv has been increasingly under aerial bombardment in recent months, putting the city on near-constant alert and disrupting daily life.

Air raid sirens warning of approaching threats in the skies sound almost round the clock, urging the city’s estimated three million people to seek shelter.

Repeated strikes on trains and petrol stations have already hit the rail and road networks while attacks on energy facilities threaten power and heating as winter approaches.

Osypenko, the seamstress, said she would not get home because of the traffic jams. Previous disruption to subway services during air raids forced her to spend the night in a metro station near the Southern Bridge.

Not being able to work costs her money, compounding the financial pressures caused by the war, she added. “You just spend the whole day feeling completely beaten down.”

The latest Russian attacks killed one person and wounded at least two other people when a 25-storey residential building was hit in southeast Kyiv.

– ‘Political will’ –

Zelensky urged tougher sanctions to prevent Russia from manufacturing its new jet-powered drones, which are faster and harder to intercept.

Russia’s production of the weapons was “critically dependent” on foreign components, he wrote on social media on Friday.

“Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries,” he added.

Zelensky has repeatedly called on Ukraine’s Western allies for more military support, particularly for US-made Patriot missile interceptors.

On Thursday, he said Ukraine had used its FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, without disclosing where or what it had been used against.

He also said Ukraine was testing five of its own interceptors against drones.

Ukraine’s military on Friday said it struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and another facility in Samara, both in southwest Russia, for allegedly supplying fuel to Russian forces.

Kyiv also dismissed reports that its F-16 fighter jets — another key tool used against jet-powered drones — could be grounded due to delays in maintenance inspection and the supply of parts.

But Zelensky told the Financial Times that around half of Ukraine’s fleet was spending lengthy maintenance periods in Europe.

World.title: Man City verdict a ‘big topic’ for England players, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said that Manchester City were the talk of the England camp after the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, but insisted that the case would not affect his selection for Saturday’s match in Croatia.

The findings by an independent commission, announced earlier this week, have sent shockwaves through English football.

City, the dominant Premier League force over the past 15 years, face severe sanctions, which could include expulsion from the top division.

Marc Guehi and Elliott Anderson are the only two City players remaining in Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League match in Rijeka after Nico O’Reilly was forced to withdraw due to injury.

“We had some time off and some time between the matches, and it’s a big subject,” Tuchel told his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“Of course the players talk about it, and City players talk about it, and we talk to them, but only briefly.

“They’re ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch and that’s what they show in camp, but of course it’s a big topic.”

City deny wrongdoing and on Friday lodged an appeal against the ruling.

But unless they can overturn the decision of the commission, they are likely to face at least a points deduction, which would threaten their place in the Premier League.

Tuchel was asked if the club’s players would still be in his mind for selection should they be playing regularly in the lower divisions.

“There’s always a possibility,” he said. “I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament, and I will never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country.

“So we need to look at this from case by case.”

England’s clash with Croatia, which will take place behind closed doors, is their third of four Nations League games in the current international window.

The Three Lions were beaten 3-2 by world champions Spain on home soil last weekend, but bounced back to beat the Czech Republic 2-0 on Tuesday.

World.title: US posts weak job growth data in September
World.content:
Washington – Employment in the United States grew by 29,000 jobs in September, missing analysts’ expectations significantly, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 4.2 percent, government data showed on Friday.

Adding to the weak data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised down job figures for July and August by a combined 60,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.

The revision to July’s data showed that the world’s largest economy lost jobs that month, as opposed to posting a gain of 21,000 as previously reported.

The data comes ahead of key midterm elections in November where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a stern test over his handling of the economy.

Analysts polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal had expected the US economy to add 84,000 jobs in September.

– Health care leads –

Employment in most major sectors was largely unchanged, the BLS reported, with health care posting notable gains of 17,000.

The sector has propped up the labor market in the United States in the last year, as an aging population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.

Still, September’s gains in the sector were slower than its average monthly gain of 33,000 over the last year.

The financial sector continued its downward slide, losing 7,000 jobs in September and bringing its overall slump from a recent peak in May 2025 to 129,000.

Most of the losses in that sector have been among insurance companies.

– Fed implications –

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.0 percent, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation — meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren seized on the data to criticize Trump’s performance since taking office last year.

“Paychecks are growing at their slowest rate in nearly seven years, outside of the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said in a statement.

“Since the start of Trump’s war, real wages have fallen 0.7 percent as his failed agenda keeps pushing prices up,” she said, referring to the US war against Iran launched in late February.

The conflict has plunged the Middle East into violence and sent global energy prices skyrocketing, as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s regional allies and choked a key trading route.

The data comes after the US Federal Reserve — which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term two-percent target while ensuring maximum employment — raised interest rates last month to address high prices.

The US labor market has been largely in balance this year, with modest job gains and a relatively steady unemployment rate.

That steadiness has allowed the Fed to focus on the inflation side of its mandate, but any weakness in the labor market may give policy makers pause.

Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

This week, two key Fed policymakers indicated that the central bank may not raise rates again at its October meeting, although markets continue to expect a further hike before the end of the year.

Friday’s jobs data “lends support to the less hawkish Fed officials that indicate no need to rush and deliver the next rate hike at the end of this month,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, in a note.

She added that this could release some pressure on bond yields — which have been spiralling in part due to expectations of interest rate hikes.

Nancy Vanden Houten at Oxford Economics, however, disagreed, expecting upside risks to inflation to continue to dominate Fed policymakers’ thinking.

“We think the upside risks to inflation are still a bigger concern for the Federal Reserve and expect they will raise rates at the end of the month,” she said.

World.title: Russia to take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, Jaishankar tells panel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister

on Saturday briefed a parliamentary consultative committee on India's "multifaceted" engagement with Russia, covering bilateral trade, investment and energy cooperation as well as New Delhi's diplomatic efforts to contribute towards ending the Ukraine conflict.

Chairing the meeting on India-Russia relations, Jaishankar also informed members that Russia has agreed to take around 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, particularly in construction and logistics, people familiar with the discussions said, according to news agency PTI.

Jaishankar said India and Russia share an ambition to expand bilateral trade in a more balanced manner, including by increasing Indian exports to Russia across seven sectors â automobiles, pharmaceuticals, food, marine products, engineering goods, chemicals and textiles.

Trade, connectivity and energy cooperation

The minister highlighted various areas of bilateral engagement, including trade, investments, energy, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties, according to a social media post by Jaishankar.

The discussions also covered an India-Eurasian Economic Union Free Trade Agreement, the Chennai-Vladivostok corridor, the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) and the Northern Sea Route.





On energy cooperation, Jaishankar said India's priority was to safeguard the interests of Indian consumers.

"Our approach is to maintain multiple sources of supply," he said, according to people familiar with the meeting.

The government has also been seeking to expand opportunities for Indian workers in Russia.

Ukraine conflict and India's diplomatic efforts

The Ukraine conflict also featured prominently in the discussions, with Jaishankar apprising the panel of India's position and recent diplomatic efforts to support dialogue and diplomacy.

In his social media post, Jaishankar said he highlighted India's "active support to dialogue & diplomacy to end the Ukraine conflict".

The minister referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's August 31 meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, where the PM said that "endless war must now give way to end of war".

Jaishankar travelled to Ukraine last month and subsequently met the foreign ministers of Ukraine and Russia in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

During those engagements, he conveyed India's readiness to assist efforts to bring the conflict to an end, people familiar with the meeting said.

"If India can be of any help in any manner to bring the war to an end, it is ready to do so," Jaishankar said in his conversations.

Putin's recent remarks at the Valdai Club in Moscow were also discussed. He had said Prime Minister Modi "has very good ideas for finding mutually acceptable solutions" to bring peace.

Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha's remarks appreciating India's efforts were also noted during the meeting.

Efforts to secure Indians in Russian military

Jaishankar also briefed the committee on the government's efforts to secure the release of Indian nationals serving in the Russian military.

NEW DELHI: A local court on Saturday granted bail to six Congress workers arrested for allegedly defacing the outer wall of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's ancestral home in Agra during a protest against alleged manipulation of voter lists.The accused - Mukesh Dhangar, Anil Yadav, Rajesh Kumar, Manoj Gaur, Rajesh Gautam and Pankaj Chaudhary - were granted bail after furnishing surety bonds of Rs 20,000 each, advocate Santosh Dixit, who represented them, said.The six were arrested on September 29 and had been sent to jail following a case registered against them under several provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including those relating to attempt to murder, rioting, wrongful restraint and assault or criminal force against a public servant.Dixit said the police had dropped Section 109(2) of the BNS, relating to attempt to murder, after failing to substantiate the charge in its submissions before the court.In an earlier hearing, the court had directed the police to conduct a detailed investigation into the invocation of Section 109(1), asking them to specify the facts, injuries, medical evidence, eyewitness testimony or other evidence supporting the charge.The court had also directed the investigating officer to complete the probe by October 3 and drop the section if the investigation did not establish the alleged offence.On September 28 protest in which some Congress workers allegedly wrote slogans with black paint on the gate and outer wall of Kumar's residence in the Vijay Nagar area of Agra.Police registered the case at Hariparvat police station on a complaint by a sub-inspector against eight named persons and 15-20 unidentified Congress workers.The other charges in the case include Section 121 of the BNS, relating to voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter a public servant from performing his duty, Section 126 on wrongful restraint and Section 132 on assault or criminal force against a public servant. Provisions relating to rioting, house-trespass, criminal intimidation and intentional insult were also invoked.Congress Agra city president Amit Singh welcomed the bail order and said the party would continue its agitation against Kumar."The serious section imposed by the police has been removed by the court. This is a victory for democracy," Singh said, adding that the Congress would continue its campaign until Kumar resigns as Chief Election Commissioner.

World.title: Akhilesh Yadav asks SP leaders to keep seat-sharing concerns internal amid friction with Congress
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(SP) president

on Saturday asked party leaders to keep their views on seat-sharing negotiations with the

within internal party channels, amid public differences between the two INDIA bloc allies ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

Yadav's intervention came after SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel publicly criticised the Congress' reported demand for 150 seats and said allocating too many constituencies to the party could affect the alliance's electoral prospects.

Addressing reporters at an event in Lucknow, Yadav said, "I would like to tell all our leaders that whatever opinions or concerns they have regarding seat-sharing should be shared with us.

Whenever the discussion takes place, we will discuss and consider their suggestions."

SP MP questions Congress' reported demand

Patel had said the Congress' reported demand for 150 seats was "highly unreasonable", pointing to the parties' performance in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

"They currently have two MLAs, whereas we have 125. Based on this ratio, they should receive seven or eight seatsâ¦ We can give them even 50 seats; anything beyond that would simply mean wasting seats and risking defeat," Patel told news agency ANI.





He said the Congress' "realistic capacity is around 25â30 seats" and stressed that the final decision on seat allocation rested with the SP national president.

"Congress should demand seats based on their actual numbers and standing, rather than making arbitrary demands. Their realistic capacity is around 25â30 seatsâ¦ Everyone knows that only Akhilesh Yadav can provide good governance, ensure justice for all, and work for the welfare of everyone.

That is why the public stands with Akhilesh Yadav; the Congress has no contribution in this regard," Patel further said.

The reported demand for at least 150 seats had also been raised by Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, who said earlier that the party had candidates available for all 403 Assembly constituencies and would not contest fewer than 150 seats under an alliance arrangement.

Congress says top leadership will decide

Newly appointed Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra said the decision on seat-sharing would be taken by the top leadership of the INDIA bloc and its constituent parties, rather than at the state level.

"Let me clarify one thing: the INDIA alliance was not formed specifically for Uttar Pradesh. It was formed in Delhi. This is not a state-level arrangement; it is a national-level alliance. Decisions regarding this will be taken by the top leadership of the alliance and the top leadership of the constituent parties," Mishra said.

She said the Congress leadership would decide both the number of seats and the timing of any alliance.

"As for the Congress party, our top leadership will decide on the number of seats and the timing of the alliance, and I am fully confident that they will do so while keeping in mind the faith and trust of Congress workers," she said.

Mishra also said Raebareli and Amethi held special significance for the Gandhi family, describing them as the family's "home".

World.title: Delhi women’s safety protests: Shivraj Chouhan reacts to viral ‘kachori-samosa’ slogans
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has reacted to viral videos from women-led protests in Delhi, questioning why women and girls have been forced to raise slogans about their safety and men.

The remarks came amid demonstrations following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old.

Chouhan referred to one of the slogans doing the rounds online, âEk kachori-do samosa, in mardo ka kya bharosaâ, and said the situation required serious consideration.

âWhy has the situation come to this, that our daughters have to chant slogans like 'One kachori, two samosas'? We must think seriously about this,â he said in a post on X, sharing a video of himself at an event.

The protests have also produced a series of rhyming slogans that have spread across social media, including, âEk kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa,â â1 jeera, 2 ajwain, mard samaj do resignâ and âThandi chai garam karo, mard jaat sharam karo.â

The slogans, which have circulated widely through Instagram, X and other platforms, have become part of the online vocabulary around the protests. The demonstrations were triggered by concerns over womenâs safety following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old at Aastha Kunj Park near Lady Shri Ram College.





Chouhan called for a collective commitment to womenâs safety and dignity.

âWe must take a resolveâ We will respect our sisters and daughters, we will ensure their safety, and we will protect their rights,â he said.

The first major demonstration was held on September 23, when around 200 students from Delhi University and affiliated institutions, including Lady Shri Ram College for Women, Miranda House, Gargi College and Dr BR Ambedkar University, took to the streets.

On September 25, hundreds of women students marched near Delhi Universityâs South Campus, demanding safer public spaces and stronger action against sexual harassment. Another demonstration was later held at the Faculty of Arts.

The protests have since been followed by measures from civic and security agencies. The Delhi Development Authority and Municipal Corporation of Delhi undertook safety audits of public parks, focusing on lighting, security personnel at entry and exit points and patrolling after sundown.

Delhi Police also stepped up patrolling across parks and other areas.

All three accused in the Aastha Kunj case have been arrested, according to PTI. One accused was pursuing a law course, whole another was arrested after an encounter with a Delhi Police.

Across our country, women are afraid to walk the streets, afraid of being harassed, afraid of being raped. And the governmentâs answer: stay at home,â Gandhi said.

Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also questioned restrictions placed on women, while chief minister Rekha Gupta said womenâs safety should not come at the cost of restricting their freedom.

NEW DELHI: The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh on Saturday said Dhakaâs extradition request for ousted ex-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was being legally examined, so New Delhi could not state a deadline for her return.âNobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasinaâs return),â High commissioner Dinesh Trivedi remarked during a discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. PTI reported.âAgain and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,â Trivedi added.Hasina sought asylum in India after a massive anti-establishment agitation led to the collapse of her government in August 2024.Trivedi said New Delhi had no role in Hasinaâs extraction. She was escorted by a Bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to India through a Bangladeshi aircraft.âAt that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on thatâ, Trivedi said.Trivedi alleged the situation emerged because of âtragic circumstancesâ in Bangladesh, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world.âWhat was our choice?â Trivedi asked, pointing at the uncertainty of the potential situation, had India denied entry to Hasinaâs aircraft.India-Bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after Hasina sought asylum in Delhi.Hasina was replaced by an interim government led by Mohammad Yunus, which repeatedly called for her extraction from India.During that 18-month interim rule, Hasina was tried in absentia by a special tribunal and sentenced to death; her Awami League party was also disbanded.Following the February 12 elections, Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) came to power. Its government endorsed the ban on Hasina's party and repeatedly renewed the demand for her extradition.However, relations never fully recovered despite a new government in Bangladesh.They were strained further when Hasina addressed a virtual press conference from New Delhi on 5 August 2026, the second anniversary of her removal from power. Bangladesh's foreign ministry had earlier said that the atmosphere for Rahman's visit had been "vitiated" by Hasina's virtual press interaction.India has maintained that it had no role in the media event and that it does not endorse anything said at the forum about the Bangladesh government.Rahman had declined the invitation to attend the BRICS outreach summit, while a separate bilateral invitation has been on hold since February.Despite the downturn in bilateral relations, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, said after meeting Trivedi on Tuesday that Dhaka was "positive" about progress in discussions on Rahman's proposed visit to India; PTI reported that no date has been fixed yet.

World.title: 'Ask cops to wear name plates': CPI MP detained during protest at Jantar Mantar writes to Amit Shah
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CPI Rajya Sabha leader P Sandosh Kumar, who was detained during a protest at Jantar Mantar on Friday, has written to Union home minister Amit Shah seeking his intervention over alleged police violence, arbitrary detentions and the concealment of identification badges by Delhi Police personnel.

The protest was held over concerns surrounding the functioning of the Election Commission of India, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, changes to Form-6 and the poll body's IT systems. Protesters had also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Kumar said he was among those detained along with workers and members of the CPI(M), CPI(ML)L, AAP, AISF, AIYF, SFI, DYFI, AISA and civil society groups.

âI was myself detained yesterday along with workers of my party, the CPI(M), CPI(ML)L, AAP, cadres of the AISF, AIYF, SFI, DYFI, AISA and members of the civil society,â Kumar said in his letter.

Kumar alleged that police had responded to peaceful protests with âviolence, mass detentions, internet shutdowns and manhandlingâ, rather than facilitating the exercise of democratic rights.

A key concern raised by the CPI leader was the alleged absence of visible name plates or identification badges on some police personnel involved in detentions and crowd-control measures.





Referring to the Supreme Court's directions in the D K Basu vs State of West Bengal case, Kumar said police personnel carrying out arrests or handling detainees were required to bear âaccurate, visible and clear identification and name tags with their designationsâ. He also cited Delhi Police Standing Order No 51, which prescribes visible name plates as part of the uniform.

âThis is not a minor procedural matter: identification is fundamental to accountability when the State exercises coercive power against citizens,â Kumar said.

Kumar also referred to reports and visual material from an earlier protest on July 20, alleging that plain-clothes personnel and officers without visible identification badges had used force against protesters.

âThe fact that the same conduct was repeated on October 2 makes the matter serious,â he said.

The CPI leader also sought an inquiry into the alleged use of facial-recognition technology at Jantar Mantar.

He referred to an investigation which, he said, found discrepancies between people identified through the system as present at a student protest and records showing some of them were already in jail in connection with criminal cases.

Kumar called for a time-bound inquiry into the use of force, alleged arbitrary detentions, concealment of identification badges, manhandling of protesters, deployment of plain-clothes personnel and use of facial-recognition systems.

He urged Shah to direct that people exercising their right to peaceful protest be protected and that police personnel deployed for crowd-control and detention duties remain identifiable.

âDemocratic dissent cannot be met with methods reminiscent of the British Raj police,â Kumar said.

âDelhi Police must understand that its duty is to protect citizens and facilitate their constitutional rights, not to intimidate, assault or silence them,â he added.

World.title: Yet another POCSO case booked against Gem Granites  Veeramani
World.content:
The Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Greater Chennai Police, which is probing the sexual assault cases against Gem Granites founder R. Veeramani, 84, has registered yet another case against him under the provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act based on a complaint from a woman in Chennai. This is the fifth case filed against him.

Meanwhile, the legal wing of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Saturday petitioned the Greater Chennai Police and the Special Investigation Team probing the case, seeking an expanded probe into the alleged suppression and cover-up of complaints of sexual assault on minor girls, including the roles of former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, former Law Minister S. Regupathy, and senior police officers.

The petition seeks to ascertain whether the complaint reached Mr. Stalin, who held the Home portfolio, and whether any directions were issued.

The petition also questions how Mr. Regupathy came to comment publicly on the quality of the video evidence in the case.

On August 29, the Immoral Trafficking Prevention Unit of the CCB arrested Veeramani on charges of sexual assaults on a minor girl, while his associates — Shanthi, 60, and Mahendra Simhan, 63 — were arrested for abetting the industrialist in the offences. The case originated in October 2025 following a receipt of a pen drive containing a video of Veeramani sexually assaulting a minor girl at a house belonging to the house of Shanthi.

Following the order of the special court for POCSO cases, the investigation picked up pace from last August. Subsequently, a fourth accused — Ganesan, who worked for 23 years at Gem Granites, was arrested on September 22 for having an obscene video of Veeramani with a minor girl on his mobile phone and failing to report it to the police. The cases against Veeramani and his associates are being investigated by a SIT led by Additional Commissioner P.C. Thenmozhi.

A senior officer of Greater Chennai Police said already four cases for offences under the POCSO Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) were booked for charges including aggravated penetrative sexual assault and abetting a minor girl to commit suicide. In addition to those cases, yet another case (fifth case) has been registered based on a complaint given by a woman who alleged that she was sexually assaulted. “More complaints are coming in, and they are being duly received. After verification, we have duly register and proceed for further action and investigation,” the officer said.

The first case was registered in October 2025 over the alleged sexual assault of a minor in 2019, followed by another POCSO case concerning an alleged sexual assault in 2024. The third case relates to the alleged sexual abuse of a Class 11 student before her suicide in 2004. The fourth case was registered on September 30 involving a minor girl.

World.title: Probe into TVK MLA driving government bus without valid licence during launch of scheme
World.content:
The Transport Department will conduct an inquiry into an incident of the TVK MLA for K.V. Kuppam Assembly constituency, E. Thendral Kumar, was seen driving a Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) bus at the new terminus, during the launch of the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme.

The action comes in the wake of public outcry after a video that was circulated in social media. The video showed Mr. Kumar driving the government bus with around 30 commuters after the launch of the scheme by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay at Koyambedu bus terminus in Chennai on Friday. “As per norms, only those drivers, who have a license to drive heavy vehicles with a badge, are eligible to drive heavy vehicles like buses. A probe will be conducted,” said a transport official.

Collector P.S. Leela Alex flagged off the buses at the terminus as part of the launch of the scheme, which expands no-fare bus travel for women and transgender persons in the State, in the presence of Vellore Corporation Commissioner A. Catherine Saranya, TVK MLA Mr. Kumar, TNSTC, and transport officials.

“It was scary as the bus that was driven by MLA Mr. Kumar was moving faster on the premises where many commuters, including women and children were waiting to board buses,” said a commuter.

Initial inquiry revealed after the flagging off of the buses by the District Collector, Mr. Kumar volunteered to drive the vehicle on the open portico of the terminus from the main entrance to a distance of around 100 metres. In the video, he was reportedly seen holding an enquiring about operating gear with the bus driver.

Transport officials said that as per norms, license holders of light vehicles were eligible to drive only cars, maxi cabs, vans, and tractors. Only those persons, who have a licence for light vehicles, can apply for a badge and a licence to drive heavy vehicles such as buses, trucks, and lorries. “In this incident, Mr. Kumar might not have the required licence and badge to drive heavy vehicles like buses. As a result, the violation will attract a penalty,” said a transport official.

As per norms, such violation by the driver will attract a fine of ₹5,000 under Motor Vehicle Act (MVA), 1988. A fine of ₹10,000 will be imposed on the owner of the vehicle. Transport officials said that based on the findings of the probe, necessary action will be taken.

World.title: Gang held in connection with murder of VCK functionary
World.content:
Four youths were arrested by Kalavai police on Saturday, in connection with the murder of a local VCK functionary.

The police said the arrested persons were identified as R. Kaviarasu, 21, B. Mani, 22, G. Sarathi, 21, and S. Dinesh, 21. They were childhood friends near Kalavai town in the district. The victim was K. Sivakumar, 60, a VCK functionary in the area.

Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, Sivakumar was returning to his house near Kalavai town on Thursday, when a gang on two-wheelers allegedly hacked him to death. On being informed, the Kalavai police inspected the spot and sent the body to Government Medical College Hospital in Vellore for postmortem.

Relatives and residents in the village staged a protest to arrest the suspects. Superintendent of Police P. Sibin pacified agitated residents, who dispersed after assurance from revenue officials and the police that they would arrest the suspects.

Special teams were formed who analysed CCTV camera footage along the route. The teams also analysed reels posted on social media, in which the gang claimed to take revenge on local political functionaries.

The police said the teams traced the location of the gang to a hideout near Arani town in Tiruvannamalai and nabbed them. The gang, led by the key suspect, Sivakumar told the police that he had a dispute over borrowed money from the victim, who allegedly threatened him with dire consequences. Angered by threats, he allegedly hacked the victim to death, along with his friends.

A case was registered. Arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore, and a probe is under way.

World.title: IUML, Jamaat-e-Islami Hind controlling UDF government, says BJP leader K. Surendran
World.content:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and the United Democratic Front (UDF) government are being “held hostage” by the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national secretary K. Surendran has said.

Addressing the media in Kozhikode on Saturday (October 3), Mr. Surendran said the Chief Minister was “prostrating himself” before the two organisations “morning and evening”.

He said the BJP had anticipated that, when the UDF government came to power, the IUML and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind would effectively run the State. “After 130 days of the government, Keralam too has realised this. Although Mr. Satheesan is at the helm of the government, the IUML and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind control it,” he alleged.

Mr. Surendran said the IUML had, for the first time, secured six Cabinet-level positions. “We have not forgotten the discussions that took place in Keralam when the IUML demanded a fifth Minister during the Oommen Chandy-led UDF government. Yet, the Muslim League has now been given five Ministers holding important portfolios, along with the new Cabinet-rank post of chairperson of the State Administrative Reforms Commission,” he said.

He alleged that the IUML had been taking decisions on matters of governance from the first day of the government. People had voted for the UDF seeking a change after the “misrule, corruption, nepotism, and administrative collapse” of the Left Democratic Front government, he said.

“Instead of the new-age Keralam that was promised, people got power cuts and unemployment. Despite promising to extend the validity of PSC rank lists, the government did not do so. The Sabarimala inquiry was completely sabotaged. Now, the government is protecting Pinarayi Vijayan and his family,” he alleged.

Mr. Surendran further alleged that the government was creating conflicts to divert attention. “The people have gained nothing. Instead, the Muslim League and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind have gained,” he said.

He also said that the government had backed down on the PM SHRI scheme under pressure from the IUML and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind.

World.title: Action proposed against use of party flags at Calicut varsity hostels
World.content:
The authorities at the University of Calicut have proposed to act against the use of political party flags and the storage of weapons at hostels on the main campus of the University of Calicut at Tenhipalam in Malappuram district.

According to sources, the issue came up for discussion at a recent meeting of the board of adjudication of students’ grievances chaired by Vice-Chancellor P. Raveendran.

There were complaints about a section of students attacking another group with lethal weapons. There is a police case related to it, too. It had been alleged that certain students’ organisations were stocking weapons at the men’s hostel. There were also reports that flags of political organisations were a notable feature on the campus. It was also alleged that the members of certain organisations were behaving as if some hostel blocks were their fiefdoms and even the wardens permitted this. The authorities have warned that criminal action would be initiated against those who violate the hostel rules. The sources said on Saturday (October 3) that the board’s proposals would be conveyed to the Syndicate, which would take a final decision on the matter.

World.title: CPI(M) district committee meeting begins at Ponnani
World.content:
The CPI(M)’s expanded district committee meeting began at Ponnani on Saturday (October 3), with the Leader of Opposition and party Politburo member Pinarayi Vijayan inaugurating the two-day session.

The meeting is focused on strengthening the party’s work among the people and planning organisational activities in response to current political conditions.

Senior leader Paloli Mohammedkutty hoisted the party flag at the RV Palace auditorium, Chamravattom. District secretary V.P. Anil presented the organisational report after the opening session.

A general discussion of the report began after group discussions and will continue on Sunday (October 4). The meeting will conclude after the leadership responds to the issues raised.

CPI(M) Central committee members P.K. Sreemathy, E.P. Jayarajan, K.K. Shailaja and C.S. Sujatha, and State secretariat members M. Swaraj and V. Sivankutty are attending.

The meeting has 135 participants, including 42 district committee members, 54 representatives from 18 area committees and 29 representatives of mass organisations.

A procession and public meeting will mark the conclusion of the programme on Sunday. The procession will begin at 4.30 p.m. from C.V. Junction near Ponnani Harbour and end at Nilayorapatha.

About 50,000 people from seven coastal area committees are expected to take part. Mr. Vijayan will inaugurate the public meeting.

World.title: Work on organ transplant institute in Kozhikode to be completed in 30 months, says Satheesan
World.content:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has said that work on the proposed Institute of Organ and Tissue Transplantation in Kozhikode will be completed in 30 months.

He was delivering a speech after opening the silver jubilee celebrations of the Kerala Heart Care Society here on Saturday (October 3). Mr. Satheesan said that ₹271 crore was being set aside for the institute coming up on a 20-acre plot in Chevayur. All the services related to organ transplantation would be brought under one roof to bring down the surgery cost to one-third. The facility would have 350 beds and 10 operation theatres. On the same premises, a dermatology hospital too had been proposed. A sum of ₹35 crore would be spent on the hospital, Mr. Satheesan said.

The institute would be elevated as a centre of excellence with a research programme attached to it. As many as 1,100 cornea transplants, 520 kidney, 50 heart, 40 lung, 120 bone marrow, 320 liver, 15 intestine, 15 pancreas, and 300 soft tissue transplant surgeries would be performed there in a year. Mr. Satheesan said that utilising the State’s climate and other advantages, Keralam would be transformed into a healthcare destination where foreigners and people from within the country could approach for treatment. Wellness centres, rehabilitation centres, and facilities providing medical treatment for stroke would be launched. An extensive campaign would soon be undertaken for prevention and early detection of diseases. K. Praveenkumar and K. Jayanth, MLAs, and K. Kunjali, president of the society, were present, among others.

The foundation stone for the proposed institute was laid by former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan in February this year. However, the work on the facility was reportedly moving at a slow pace after the change of government.

World.title: Kannada cinema has a new headache: Paid reviews
World.content:
On social media, the pattern is often predictable when a prominent Kannada film hits the screens: a bunch of posts flood X (formerly Twitter), describing how good the movie is. The stock phrases range from “Kannada cinema goes to the next level” to “epic climax”. Insiders to the industry identify these as markers of the disturbing trend of “paid reviews”.

Influencer culture is making its presence felt in the film industry, and campaigns are meticulously planned. The film team decides what goes out, down to every word, in a WhatsApp group. The public relations (PR) team then identifies a bunch of X users with a decent number of subscribers and pays them to share tweets favouring the movie, say insiders of the industry. The same goes for Instagram promotions, where people identifying as “film reviewers” and “experts” provide reviews for a price.

A PR official, on condition of anonymity, told The Hindu that paid reviews and posts are seen as yet another marketing technique. “It is like a new restaurant or a dish. A critic may not prefer it, but a section of the audience will be interested to try them out. Continuous tweets, posts, and videos are meant to reach those people, so that they can go check out the movie.”

This approach to marketing is increasingly being called out by cinephiles who crave objective reviews. “You see 10–20 posts with similar wording. It’s easy to guess that the reviews aren’t genuine,” says S.S. Ravikumar, an upcoming filmmaker active on social media.

But these “orchestrated reviews” do not always work, says Pavithra Gowda, co-founder of the PR agency Pink Tickets. “A film can only sustain and win at the box office if its content resonates with the audience.” In the long run, paid reviews will affect an artist’s or a filmmaker’s reputation when the movie eventually fails to connect with the audience.

Taking a different route for promotion, the Raj B. Shetty-produced Su From So, one of the biggest hits of 2025, had paid-premiere shows in four-five cities of Karnataka before it hit the screens worldwide. The idea, as explained by Raj, was to skip the routine route of press conferences, interviews, and trailer-launch events, and take the film directly to people.

The formula worked, as organic word-of-mouth spread like wildfire. However, several films that followed the Su From So model tried to manipulate it. They created plenty of videos showing rapturous responses at the premiere shows, with paid and non-paid influencers forming part of the crowd. It was clear that the film teams were desperate to project that the movie had impressed fans. “The response can be confusing, making the audience lose the ability to distinguish between a paid promotion, personal opinion, and an honest review,” admits Ravikumar.

S. Shivakumar, veteran film critic and writer, says that paid reviews were not an uncommon phenomenon in the pre-social media era either, though they have changed form and reach now. “Of course, some accepted, and some didn’t,” he says.

A PR’s job is not simply about blindly pushing a movie, says Harish Arasu, founder of PR company Arasu Creations. “There will be many small-scale movies with great content. The producers won’t have the budget to market the movies,” he says, underlining the need to find novel ways to reach a wide audience. Negative campaigns also hurt the prospects of movies, he adds.

ALSO READ: ‘Bail’ movie review: Shivarajkumar anchors a passable crime drama

Kairam Vaashi, film critic, concurs that paid negative campaigns are equally dangerous. “They choke a movie before it gets a chance to blossom in its first week,” he says.

With the Kannada audience showing great reluctance to come to theatres except on rare occasions, the film industry is exploring every possible way to catch their attention. However, with paid reviews becoming more prevalent, the industry will have to look at other creative means to draw people to movies, especially as word-of-mouth is slowly becoming the deciding factor in a movie’s fate.

World.title: Official outcome of govt-opposition talks awaited after hours-long meeting
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A second round of talks between the government and the opposition was held on Saturday to discuss various issues, with the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad being the most prominent matter.

The meeting at Parliament House, which began shortly before 5pm, went on for over four hours. However, with both sides seemingly agreeing not to speak to the media before matters conclude, official details on the outcome are still awaited.

Visuals broadcast by DawnNewsTV after the meeting showed Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi — part of the government delegation — departing Parliament House with a document in his hand, with media reports suggesting he was likely to consult the president.

The meeting, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. The dialogue comes ahead of the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government.

As the huddle began, the NA speaker expressed his hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as Friday’s, according to a post on the NA’s X account.

The government side included Naqvi, Minister for States and Frontier Regions Amir Muqam, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry.

Senator Sherry Rehman, along with MNAs Syed Naveed Qamar and Aijaz Hussain Jakhrani, represented the PPP.

The opposition delegation comprised Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI interim chairman Gohar Ali Khan, Opposition Chief Whip Amir Dogar, MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh.

KP CM adamant on long march

Earlier in the day, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi voiced his determination to hold the long march on Oct 4 and vowed to prevent a repeat of the events of May 9, 2023.

In response, Chaudhry said the KP CM’s statements could affect the ongoing negotiation process and urged PTI leaders not to engage in such discourse.

In his post, CM Afridi said PTI was the largest and most popular political party in Pakistan. “Pakistan is a democratic country whose Constitution grants us the right to peaceful protest.”

Detailing his long march plan, Afridi said an “ocean of people” would begin its journey from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4.

The party would continue its struggle until the supremacy of the Constitution and the law was ensured in Pakistan and an independent judiciary was restored, the PTI leader added.

“All demands of the PTI are in accordance with the constitution and the law.”

He stressed that the party would “neither allow May 9 to happen again nor allow anyone else to repeat it”.

Reacting to the KP CM’s remarks, Chaudhry said Afridi’s statements could affect the ongoing negotiation process even though the government wanted them to be “meaningful and fruitful”.

He urged PTI leaders to refrain from making such statements until the final stage of the negotiations, so that the dialogue process was not “harmed”.

“The language that Sohail Afridi is using against his opponents and our leadership does not seem like that of a chief minister; his statements are extremely indecent and reprehensible,” Chaudhry said.

Speaking to reporters ahead of the meeting, PPP’s Rehman stressed that her party was making efforts to solve issues in a democratic manner.

Asked about KP CM being adamant on the PTI march, the PPP leader said it was up to the PTI, but added that she would refrain from making comments before the talks conclude.

While acknowledging that each party had its positions, she noted that the objective of holding negotiations was to “discuss those positions”.

Opposition decides SOPs

Prior to the meeting with the government, the opposition held a meeting in which standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the talks were finalised.

It was decided that it would be proposed during the meeting that no one from either side would speak to the media during the talks and that a joint statement would be issued afterwards to avoid any misunderstanding.

Talking to Dawn, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousufzai said comments made by PPP leader Sherry Rehman on Friday had triggered a controversy, leaving the situation unpleasant until late at night.

“The opposition alliance held a meeting before the start of the talks, during which the government side’s views regarding the law and order situation in KP were discussed. After consultation with the KP chief minister, a response was prepared, which will be presented to the government side during the meeting today,” he said.

Replying to a question, Akhunzada said it was also decided that it would be proposed during the meeting that no one would issue a media statement regarding the dialogue and that a joint statement would be issued after the meeting.

He said the joint statement would reduce chances of confusion and differences of opinion.

‘Political solutions to political problems’

In a post on X on Friday, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, an ally of the PML-N government, pressed PTI to unconditionally call off the long march, which, he said, would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and threats emanating from neighbouring countries.

Bilawal also welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”.

Meanwhile, PTI KP Secretary Information Shaukat Yousafzai said on Friday that the party’s protest march would start from the southern districts and be led by CM Afridi.

“The march on October 4 will take place at any cost,” he said in a statement.

Also on Friday, the army’s top brass warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”.

For the first time in almost three years, representatives of the federal government and the opposition PTI formally came together on Friday for talks aimed at easing the political tension in the country, and apprised each other of their positions.

Though neither side shared its specific demands with the media, both were hopeful of a positive outcome from the meeting.

Sources on both sides told Dawn that the PTI wants its incarcerated founder Imran Khan to be shifted from jail to a hospital for medical treatment, while the government has insisted that the opposition call off its protest march on Islamabad.

In August, PTI announced a long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of Imran. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4.

Emergency option

The talks come as the PTI remains resolute on the march. Federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while the PTI has warned of dire consequences if such a step is taken.

The decision to hold talks was taken on Thursday at a presidency meeting attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Mr Naqvi, Attorney General Mansoor Awan and other PPP and PML-N leaders.

A source privy to the huddle told Dawn the emergency option was discussed, but participants agreed to first give the opposition a chance to settle matters peacefully through dialogue, and to seriously consider an emergency only if the PTI did not back down. The coalition also believes the march will remain confined to KP and not enter Punjab or Islamabad.

On Thursday, Sanaullah said the government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” over the protest, and that the decision on the march rested with the PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”. “So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned.

Separately, the prime minister has invited Achakzai for dialogue, and the two are expected to meet in the coming days.

World.title: Bilawal says Centre was ready to impose emergency in KP but PPP sought 'political solution'
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Saturday said the federal government had made up its mind to impose emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; however, his party suggested finding a political solution to fight terrorism in a “better way”.

Addressing an event in Karachi, Bilawal said that the federal government had been in contact with President Asif Ali Zardari and the PPP regarding the recent security situation, particularly in KP.

Noting the terrorist attacks emanating from Afghanistan, Bilawal said, “In my opinion, the federal government had made up its mind and was 100 per cent ready; they wanted to immediately impose emergency or governor’s rule in KP.”

He noted that although imposing governor’s rule or emergency in any province was a Constitutional tool, the PPP “was of the view that before dropping this constitutional atomic bomb, political parties should absolutely find a political solution to fight terrorism in a better way”.

Sharing his party’s view, Bilawal said the PPP wanted to hold talks with the protesting party — the PTI — regarding its planned Oct 4 long march to Islamabad before making any decision.

While calling on all parties to engage in dialogue with PTI before imposing emergency, he also urged the latter to abandon its long march to Islamabad and acknowledge the success of their protest.

Bilawal said the PTI protest had been somewhat successful as the capital “has been shut for 10 days”, even if the party had not marched towards it. “A political party or worker should see that you have achieved success on the political stage.”

However, he pointed out: “But it is also correct that while you are focusing on your own politics, there is terrorist activity in KP every other day.

“If the provincial government does not consider this issue of terrorism and law and order important, and there are allegations that they are not standing with the federation, then we may be forced to declare an emergency or governor’s rule.”

The PPP chief noted that the terrorist threat from Afghanistan and India’s “hideous role” in supporting it was apparent. “Do not see terrorism through a political lens.”

“We want to come together to fight terrorism and not view it as a political issue, but a national one,” Bilawal emphasised, recalling a recent meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Zardari.

The Bhutto scion called for a written agreement between the KP and federal governments which would outline “how they will combat terrorism together”.

“If there is any political deadlock, it needs to be kept separate from issues like terrorism or national interests.”

The government and PPP are jointly engaged in talks with the opposition, aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis.

The discussions precede the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government.

The decision to have talks with the opposition was taken after PM Shehbaz called on President Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr in Islamabad earlier this week. National security, institutional cooperation on law and order and the possibility of using emergency powers were among the topics discussed.

A joint delegation comprising PML-N and PPP leaders met the opposition on Friday, with a second round of talks held on Saturday. As the politicians gathered at Parliament House, National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq expressed hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as the day before.

Bilawal announces water projects for Karachi’s SITE

Earlier in his speech, Bilawal congratulated the people of Karachi on the completion of a water project and added that the PPP saw its first success in local government elections.

“We have started a 35m gallon water treatment project, and this water will fulfil the needs of SITE,” he stated.

“The dirty water that used to pollute Karachi, our sea and our river will be treated, bringing benefits for all. In the second phase, 65 million gallons will be treated by January. Once this is completed, the capacity will reach 100 million gallons.”

“The number one priority for us is water. Eight per cent of Sindh’s water comes through Irsa,” Bilawal said, referring to the Indus River System Authority, which releases water downstream into Sindh. However, persistent water shortages due to Irsa not releasing sufficient water have triggered strong protests in the past.

He said Karachi and Sindh “do not get our deserved share” as the 1991 Water Apportionment Accord has not been implemented. “Rather than giving us water, they pursue projects without our permission, which causes water shortages in Sindh and Karachi.

“The Sindh government and KMC (Karachi Metropolitan Corporation) prioritised saving water for the people of Karachi, so that they can avail extra water,” Bilawal outlined, adding that several months ago, a 25m gallon water treatment facility was inaugurated in Kemari.

“As the mayor told you, the capacity will be increased by 55 million gallons, so that we can deliver those benefits to the people of Kemari,” he added.

Calling it the first project of its kind in Pakistan, Bilawal expressed hope that the needs of people in Karachi’s SITE area would be met, noting that it is the “engine” for the economy of the city and Pakistan.

Additionally, the PPP chief noted that by Oct 20, projects to provide 10m gallons of water to Lyari and the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) through a pipeline would be completed.

World.title: Local automakers voice concerns as imports of used cars surge in Sept
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Imports of used cars surged in September after easing of regulations, inviting criticism from local manufacturers while importers claim that the move will bring competition in the auto sector.

After a brief decline due to the government abolishing the Pers­onal Baggage Scheme and applying restrictions to control misuse of used car schemes for overseas Pakistanis, imports of used cars have started surging again.

In the month of September, a total of 2,276 vehicles were imported under the Gift Scheme as the strict restrictions under the Baggage Scheme continue, according to data from the Commerce Ministry.

The figures show that in May, only 48 used cars were imported mainly through the baggage scheme. However, the situation started to change from June onwards.

In June, a total of 843 vehicles were imported, including 806 under the Gift Scheme. The figure reached 1,938 in July, with 1,876 cars under the Gift Scheme.

August saw a total of 1,445 vehicle imports, while 2,276 vehicles were imported in September, with 2,238 under the Gift Scheme.

A senior executive of the auto industry noted that the reduction in duties on completely built units (CBUs) by 20-25 per cent in the 2026-27 budget has reduced the import cost.

“We have reports that a one-year restriction on transfer of ownership is not being implemented in some cities, due to which this business is flourishing again, but at the cost of the domestic auto industry which consists of 13 assemblers and over 300 auto parts manufacturers,” the executive added.

Auto parts vendors expressed their concerns too, claiming that auto production had finally begun to show an increase after a gap of three years, which was also contributing to Pakistan’s growth in the large-scale manufacturing (LSM) sector.

“Locally produced cars contain up to 60pc local parts by value, amounting to an average of Rs1.5 million per vehicle, and import of 2,276 used vehicles meant loss of Rs3.4 billion of local parts production which creates jobs and operates in the documented economy,” said Abdul Rehman Aizaz, chairman of Pakistan Asso­ciation of Automotive Parts and Ac­­cessories Manufacturers (Paa­pam).

He termed it unfair that, on the one hand, the proposed auto policy was slashing import duties on new cars, while on the other hand, imports of used cars were being encouraged.

“Ultimately, Pakistan is moving towards a market dominated by imported new and used vehicles with no industrial activity,” the Paapam chairman said, terming the business of used cars completely unregulated.

Competition in auto sector

On the contrary, importers claim that Pakistan needs to have a competitive economy and that importing used cars was completely legal if done as per the government regulations.

“Currently, all imported vehicles are subjected to pre-shipment inspections by the accredited companies based in Japan as most of the used cars are imported from that country,” said Mian Shaoib Ahmed, chairman of All Pakistan Car Dealers & Importers Association.

Ahmed, also a member of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry’s (FPCCI) executive committee, stressed there was a demand for used cars in Pakistan.

He contended that new Chinese entrants have yet to make their mark in Pakistani markets, while Japanese car assemblers in the country were not yet ready for the competitive environment.

The FPCCI member lauded the government for recent changes in the vehicle import regime and added that used car imports under the Gift Scheme and commercial imports will continue to rise in the coming months.

Ahmed referred to a notification by the Engineering Development Board (EDB), dated Sep 30, which would relax the criteria for imports of used vehicles.

The changes in the recent EDB notification against the earlier notification included the removal of a clause for the minimum capital requirement of a company importing used cars, and now, any tax-registered individual or firm not even registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) can import vehicles.

The pre- and post-shipment inspection will be conducted through the Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority (PSQCA) instead of the EDB.

However, the PSQCA chief executive officer said that inspection was not done directly under or by the authority, but through its registered inspection agencies.

Currently, only two local inspection agents have been registered with the PSQCA; they are the representatives of firms accredited with the Japanese Foreign Principals Inspection Agencies.

World.title: Efforts underway to repatriate remains of 3 Pakistanis killed while recovering hijacked tanker from Somali pirates: PMO
World.content:
The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) on Saturday said that arrangements were underway to repatriate the remains of three Pakistani sailors, who were killed during an operation earlier this week to recover a hijacked oil tanker off the coast of Somalia.

The maritime police force of Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland said on Tuesday that it had recovered the MT Honour 25, a Palau-flagged oil tanker with 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis.

The Foreign Office confirmed on Wednesday that three Pakistanis had died and three others were injured during the operation, later identifying the deceased as Rafiullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari.

According to a statement by the PMO issued on Saturday, arrangements were being made to repatriate the sailors’ remains as per the instructions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

The remains had been taken to Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa, with Ethiopian Airlines reviewing the next steps for transferring the bodies.

“Following this, final approval will be granted for their departure on a flight bound for Karachi. In accordance with the prime minister’s instructions, the relevant authorities are in continuous contact to expedite the repatriation process,” the statement read.

It added that the premier had assured of “all possible assistance” in bringing the deceased sailors home.

PM Shehbaz has announced a relief package worth Rs12.5 million for the deceased sailors’ families, the PMO said yesterday.

The prime minister announced financial support for the families of the deceased, including free housing and free education for their children. The PMO added that the premier spoke with Syed Kashif Umer’s son, Azhan Kashif, on the phone to extend his condolences and express his grief.

Yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that four of the 10 Pakistani crew members had been “safely retrieved” and were scheduled to arrive in Karachi today.

The four crew members — Yasir Khan, Aqeel Khan, Amin bin Shams and Usman Ghani — were retrieved following “sustained efforts” by FO and Pakistan’s embassy in Djibouti, Dar said.

Months with no progress

The MT Honour 25 had been hijacked by Somali pirates on April 21, around 30 nautical miles off Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland region. Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan.

For around five months, there had been no progress either in negotiations or in the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages, despite concerns abounding about their declining health.
